LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. away.blurb: The Patriots' three-game win streak is over after they ran out of time and luck in their 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. Safety Kevin Byard departed after he was checked out by trainers with 9:44 left in the second quarter before returning. Defensive tackle Christian Barmore departed late in the game with an undisclosed ailment. But for a team that came in dealing with multiple injuries, including being down two starters on the offensive line, coach Mike Vrabel left Soldier Field feeling disappointed in the outcome, but not downtrodden about the resolve of his team going forward. “We fought. I would say that we need to (force opponents to) turn the ball over and tackle better and those are fundamental skills. But I like the way they competed and we certainly gave ourselves a chance,” Vrabel said. With left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) joining right guard Mike Onwenu (ankle) on injured reserve this week, the Patriots went with recent addition Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse in their places. home.headline: Report: Bears Fear Cole Kmet’s Knee Injury Is Season-Ending
home.blurb: The Cole Kmet injury that knocked him out of Thursday night's game now threatens to cost the Chicago Bears their top blocking tight end for the rest of the season. Chicago is 5-2 and sits as the No. 5 seed in the NFC, so a hole in the middle of its offense matters to every team chasing it in the NFC North, Detroit included. Kmet left Thursday's win over the New England Patriots with a knee injury and did not return. On Friday morning, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that the early read is grim: "#Bears TE Cole Kmet, who was carted off in last night's win over the #Patriots, is believed to have suffered a serious, likely season-ending knee injury, sources say. Kmet is undergoing testing this morning, and until those results come back, there is no finality." Report: Bears Fear Cole Kmet’s Knee Injury Is Season-Ending - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on Report: Bears Fear Cole Kmet’s Knee Injury Is Season-Ending Glenn Kaplan Fri, October 23, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads What Chicago Loses Without Its Top Blocker Kmet had caught just 10 passes for 87 yards and a touchdown on 14 targets this season, averaging 8.7 yards per reception, so Chicago is not losing a volume target in the passing game. It is losing the tight end it leans on to block. The Bears like to run a lot of two tight end sets, and Kmet's absence will show up most in that part of the offense. Colston Loveland is still there as the bigger receiving threat, and Chicago should still be a playoff team. Why the Cole Kmet Injury Matters to Sam LaPorta and the Lions Detroit has its own tight end question. Sam LaPorta is in the final season of his rookie contract and is set to be an unrestricted free agent in 2027 after extension talks with the Lions broke off in early October. That has made his future one of the loudest stories on the beat this week, right alongside the rest of Detroit's approach to the trade deadline . All trading for 2026 ends at 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10 , so if the Lions were ever going to move LaPorta, that is the window. After the season the choices are a new deal, the franchise tag, or letting him hit the market. A division rival suddenly thin at tight end is the kind of thing that gets floated, and Detroit has done this before. The Lions sent T.J. Hockenson to the Minnesota Vikings at the 2022 deadline. Doing it again with Chicago would be wild, and it feels highly unlikely this time around. The Minnesota Vikings lead the division at 5-0 and hold the No. 2 seed in the NFC . Chicago is fifth at 5-2, the Green Bay Packers are sixth at 4-2, and Detroit is seventh at 3-2. The Lions host Green Bay on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, and that game will say more about Detroit's October than anything happening at tight end in Chicago.

But for a team that came in dealing with multiple injuries, including being down two starters on the offensive line, coach Mike Vrabel left Soldier Field feeling disappointed in the outcome, but not downtrodden about the resolve of his team going forward. “We fought. I would say that we need to (force opponents to) turn the ball over and tackle better and those are fundamental skills. But I like the way they competed and we certainly gave ourselves a chance,” Vrabel said. With left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) joining right guard Mike Onwenu (ankle) on injured reserve this week, the Patriots went with recent addition Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse in their places. Quarterback Drake Maye was sacked twice, but the 10th different offensive line combination the Patriots have used this season held up well. Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards and two TDs and a rushing score. But after the loss he put the onus on himself to make better decisions, namely his costly second-quarter interception in the end zone when he was trying to complete a pass to tight end Eli Raridon. The Bears scored on their ensuing drive to take a 20-7 lead. “I thought we battled the environment well,” Maye said. "And I thought we did some good things but didn’t execute at a high enough level to win.” Despite the loss, New England's offense didn't show much regression overall. Maye had the one interception, but it was was on a pass in the red zone. The running game took a step back. The Patriots rushed for just 70 yards after entering the night averaging 130.7 yards per game on the ground. Though they were playing catch-up for most of the night, it made the offense a lot more predictable in the second half, allowing the Bears to drop more players into coverage. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson. He finished with five catches for 93 yards, including pulling in a short pass from Maye and rumbling 48 yards for a touchdown on the final play of the first half to cut Chicago's lead to 20-14. It marked his fifth career career TD reception. Rookie edge rusher Gabe Jacas. Trailing 13-7 in the second quarter, Caleb Williams connected on a pass with Luther Burden for a 22-yard gain. But Jacas was called for roughing the passer for an extremely late hit on Williams. It added an additional 15 yards to give Chicago the ball on the New England 33. The Bears scored five plays later on a 24-yard TD pass from Williams to Burden. Minus-7 — That's the Patriots turnover differential through seven games. Only Indianapolis (minus-8 through six games) is worse. The Thursday night game gives the Patriots a little extra time to rest and prepare before

All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (+3.5) Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons (+3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans (+1.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16 Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset. Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18 Miami Dolphins (+4.5) at New York Jets The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. Pick: Cowboys 21, Eagles 20 New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. The call is that one pass is tipped and picked off in the second half, while another is forced into coverage on a late drive. Those turnovers would turn a competitive game into a Steelers cushion. There is a counterpoint. Shough has produced touchdowns despite modest yardage, so this prediction depends on game script more than on his recent efficiency. Chris Olave posts 120 yards and two touchdowns in a losing rally Olave had double-digit targets in each of the first four games. Over the last two he has seen only 13 targets, producing an 8-89-1 line. That drop in volume looks like the sort of dip that corrects itself. Pittsburgh's defense will give him room to correct it. Pittsburgh still holds on. The prediction is Steelers 31, Saints 27, with Boswell's late field goal sealing it. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints' receiving group could be even more dangerous. For the first time in the league's long existence, a regular season game will be played in France. Paris, to be exact. After nearly 20 years since the Dolphins and Giants played the first regular season game outside of North America, the NFL's international footprint grows larger every year. As interesting as all of that is, the football played on the field is what really matters. Pittsburgh enters Week 7 with a 4-2 record, barely beating the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime a week ago. The Saints, meanwhile, climbed to 2-4 after a bizarre 34-27 win over the Giants. Both teams have plenty of flaws they are hoping to correct as the season goes on, but the Steelers are favored for a reason. As the game approaches, we will have all of the important details you need to know. Injury reports, weather reports, how to watch, storylines, and more. So bookmark this page and come back throughout the week! How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints in Week 7 Date: Sunday, October 25 Time: 9:30 a.m. EST TV Network: NFL Network Announcers: Dave Pasch (Play-by-Play), Kurt Warner and Jason Kelce (Color Analysts), Molly McGrath (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 7 Steelers injury reports will appear here as they become available New Orleans Saints Injury Report for Week 7 Saints injury reports will appear here as they become available Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints Week 7 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: TBD Wind Speed: TBD Precipitation: TBD Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 7 Will the Steelers continue leaning on the passing game despite missing multiple playmakers? Despite missing multiple receivers heading into their Week 6 matchup with the Buccaneers, the Steelers chose to make the passing game the focal point of the offense. While they ultimately came away with the victory, it was an ugly mess for much of the contest. Aaron Rodgers put up a solid 253 yards through the air, but it took him a whopping 49 pass attempts to get there. He was the definition of a checkdown merchant , with just five of those 49 passes traveling beyond 10 yards, according to Next Gen Stats . It seemed as though Mike McCarthy didn't have faith that Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle could succeed against the Buccaneers' stout run defense. Still, the Steelers can't win games against good teams with that offensive approach. The Saints could be a team that they can once again get away with it against, but it's something to monitor. Which team will handle the international trip better? There has been plenty of discourse surrounding how to handle playing across the pond ever since the NFL's International Series took shape. We saw the Rams be criticized for arriving in Australia right before their Week 1 disaster against the 49ers, who had been down under for days at that point. In the Steelers case, they are taking the route of trying to make the week feel as normal as possible, choosing to fly out on Thursday evening. Meanwhile, the Saints arrived in France on Monday, so they will be well adjusted by game time on Sunday. Will the contrasting strategies make any difference? Only time will tell. Can the Steelers pass rush come alive against a struggling Saints offensive line? The Steelers' pass rush has long been the strength of their defense, but they haven't been as effective on a down-to-down basis this season. According to Sumer Sports , Pittsburgh ranks just 23rd in pressure percentage at 37.4%. They do rank ninth in sacks with 16, so they have managed to get the QB on the ground at an above-average level. Still, they aren't causing as much disruption as they need to be, considering the names in that group. T.J. Watt has cooled off after a hot start, Alex Highsmith isn't having his best season, and Nick Herbig has made splash plays but hasn't been as dominant as he was last season. The interior has been hot and cold, with Cam Heyward remaining a consistent presence while the other pieces have been hit-or-miss. With the Saints missing star left tackle Kaleb Banks, this is an opportunity for them to really hit their stride. If they don't, it may be time to worry. away.headline: Steelers' TJ Watt pops up on injury report with new concern
away.blurb: The former Defensive Player of the Year didn’t practice on Wednesday for a rest designation. But, then he was limited in practice on Thursday because of a calf injury. This is a new injury to the public. There was some good defensive news coming out of the Steelers’ injury report, though. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday after not practicing the day prior with a wrist injury, so that was improvement. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was also limited with a groin issue, the same designation as Wednesday. Related Articles Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Pittsburgh Steelers haven’t been able to catch a break from injuries the last few weeks. It seems like a new star player is being added to the injury report each week. Thursday’s injury report included a surprising name, one that Steelers fans wish wasn’t on the list: edge rusher T.J. Watt. It’s unclear when or how Watt suffered the calf injury. But, now there’s a possibility, even if just a slight one, that Watt could miss Sunday’s game in Paris against the New Orleans Saints . Watt being absent for a game is always a loss for the Steelers. He can always make big and important plays for his team. Through six games this season, Watt’s recorded 4.5 sacks (tied for eighth in the league), 15 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. Veteran tackle Cameron Heyward didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday for rest designations, but he should be good to go come Sunday. Safety DeShon Elliott recorded his second-straight full practice on Thursday, meaning he’ll likely play on Sunday. It would mark Elliott’s first game since last October after he suffered an MCL sprain, hyperextended knee and a hamstring injury. away.headline: Veteran Steelers Safety on Track to Be Activated for Sunday in Paris
away.blurb: Eligible to be activated two weeks ago, veteran safety DeShon Elliott still needed more time to ramp up for a return from the combination of a hamstring and knee injury that forced him to open the season on injured reserve. However, now two weeks later and without any recent setbacks, it appears Elliott is on track to play this weekend. Out with a severe hamstring tear and hyperextended knee, the Steelers placed Elliott on injured reserve at the start of the season, forcing him to at least miss the team's first four games, and he's now missed two more since. A sixth-round pick of the rival Baltimore Ravens in 2018, Elliott, now 29, a consensus All-American out of the University of Texas, has recorded 433 tackles, forced six fumbles and recovered five in 77 games and 69 starts across seven healthy seasons out of his eight years in the league. He spent a season each with the Detroit Lions and Miami Dolphins before joining the Steelers in 2024. Elliott made a career-high 108 combined tackle in his first season in Pittsburgh in 2024, but was only able to register 38 in five games last year. Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. "Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar," Knox wrote. "Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles." Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline.

away.blurb: Saints Injury Report: Cesar Ruiz out again Thursday ahead of Steelers game – Crescent City Sports menu The New Orleans Saints continued preparations for Sunday's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Thursday, with starting right guard Cesar Ruiz remaining sidelined by a knee injury and kicker Daniel Carlson still absent for personal reasons. Ruiz, who sustained the injury during Sunday's 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, did not participate in Thursday's practice after also missing Wednesday's session. His availability is a significant concern for a Saints offensive line preparing to face Pittsburgh's defensive front in Paris. Carlson also missed another practice after not traveling with the Saints to France. Instead, he awaits the arrival of his newborn child. Head coach Kellen Moore previously indicated that the kicker was expected to join the team before Sunday's game. Practice squad kicker Charlie Smyth remains a potential option if Carlson cannot return in time. The Saints added defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to Thursday's report as a non-injury-related rest designation. He did not practice. There was encouraging news elsewhere on the injury report. Quarterback Tyler Shough continued to participate fully despite dealing with a left-hand injury. Backup quarterback Spencer Rattler, who was added to the report with a knee injury Thursday, also practiced fully. Running back C.J. Donaldson was upgraded to full participation after being limited Wednesday with a shoulder injury. Cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry (head) and defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness) also practiced fully. Linebackers Anfernee Jennings (knee) and Kaden Elliss (calf) remained limited, as did running back Alvin Kamara, who is managing a back injury. Elliss' potential return would be particularly important as the linebacker has missed the previous three games while dealing with the calf injury. He has expressed optimism about playing against Pittsburgh. More clarity should come on Friday with the final injury report. The Week 7 game is apoears to be pivotal. Entering the bye week 3-4 and on a win streak versus 2-5 may the difference for New Orleans between making a push in the NFC South or a disappointing campaign. The Saints face the Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France, with kickoff scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Central time in part of the NFL's international series. Penix has been a boost to the Atlanta offense, but back-to-back losses have the Falcons chasing Carolina in the NFC South standings. Does that hurt them against an Atlanta team that has some elite weapons on Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts? The Falcons defense has been the issue the past two weeks in losses to Baltimore and Chicago, and it has a tough matchup with the No. 2 team in EPA/Play this season. I also have some concerns about Michael Penix Jr. After a few strong starts to begin his 2026 season, his accuracy issues have shown up again, and his completion percentage over expected numbers has been dreadful the past two weeks. The Falcons are in over their head in this game, and I'm surprised the line is set at just a field goal. The 49ers have been banged up all season long, but it doesn’t seem to matter who Kyle Shanahan plugs in to this offense, Brock Purdy is going to make it work. Atlanta was torched by the Bears in the first half of their Week 6 loss, and it’s starting to look like the Falcons’ “turnaround” was far from what we should expect from this team in 2026. Atlanta has already dropped out of the top 10 in EPA/Play on defense, and I don’t expect it to slow down a 49ers team that is third in the league in yards per play and No. 2 in points scored in 2026. picks.blurb: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Former Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster. The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta. San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons. If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener. Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie. Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization. The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September. Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure. The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad . Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay. For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender. Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two. Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen. The San Francisco 49ers opened as 4.5-point road favorites following their win over Washington on Monday. Early opinions have trimmed as many as two points off that spread, pushing through the key number of 3. If you read my Week 7 NFL Underdogs column, you know I grabbed Atlanta +3.5 earlier in the week. With the Falcons now trading at +2.5, I see more worth in their outright price rather than taking less than a field goal (underdogs of +2.5 or shorter are 12-13 SU and ATS this season). On top of injuries stacking up for the 49ers, specifically at receiver, this venture to Georgia is just San Francisco's second true road game of the season. A good chunk of the Niners' positive power ratings are produced by those home-friendly results. This is also an early wake-up call for the 49ers, who take the field at 10 a.m. PT in Atlanta and do so on a short week , after playing on Monday in Week 6. There is also a looming look-ahead for a banged-up roster, with a bye waiting in Week 8. The Falcons are being downgraded for a sloppy loss to Chicago last weekend, in which Atlanta had three turnovers and less than 20 minutes of possession. Still, the Falcons were threatening a fourth-quarter. 49ers vs Falcons combo If you like a short underdog, often times the moneyline is worth a wager. Atlanta stays home while the 49ers travel for an early kickoff on a short week. Robinson is a workhorse for Atlanta and could see an even bigger snap share with fellow RB Brian Robinson dealing with a hamstring injury. But a San Francisco defense that tops the league in defensive expected points added per play on rushing attempts will be in for its stiffest test yet against the All-Pro ball carrier. On the other side of the ball, Brock Purdy will look to maintain sky-high efficiency despite mounting attrition at wide receiver . Falcons vs 49ers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: 49ers -4.5 Moneyline: 49ers -230; Falcons +190 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Falcons vs 49ers USA TODAY expert picks Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: 49ers 35, Falcons 24 How San Francisco's surprising defense handles Robinson is sure to be one of the most compelling storylines in this game. But mitigating any damage might not fall on that unit alone. Chicago managed to minimize Robinson's role by stringing together long drives and holding onto the ball for more than 40 minutes. Given how prolific San Francisco's offense is at working the intermediate area - and how badly Atlanta's defense struggles in that area - the 49ers could leave the Falcons in a problematic position by racing out to an early lead and controlling the terms of the game. Adam Kaufman: 49ers 30, Falcons 23 At some point, San Francisco's injuries have to catch up with it, right? The 49ers keep answering that question with another win to stay unbeaten, although Mike Evans' latest injury creates another challenge on a short week before traveling to Atlanta. Fortunately, Brock Purdy still has Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle to help keep the offense moving. I like those options against a Falcons secondary that has struggled. The Falcons' path is straightforward: feed Bijan Robinson, keep Purdy watching and prevent Michael Penix Jr. from having to rescue the game with difficult throws. That should keep Atlanta competitive, but I'm still expecting San Francisco to execute more consistently and take advantage of a mistake or two. Will McFadden Senior Reporter FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Atlanta Falcons will look to break their two-game skid against one of the NFL's three remaining undefeated teams when the San Francisco 49ers come to town for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on Sunday. Injuries have become a storyline for both teams, particularly for Atlanta's defense and San Francisco's offense, and there could be some important game-time decisions. Nevertheless, there is plenty of familiarity between these coaching staffs and star power on these rosters. As was the case in Week 5, when the Falcons faced the Baltimore Ravens, this game will feature two of the league's preeminent running backs in Bijan Robinson and Christian McCaffrey. The 49ers are also led offensively by quarterback Brock Purdy, who is playing arguably the best football of his career so far this season. "The more you watch him, the more you just appreciate the player that he is," Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said of Purdy. "He does everything well. And that's the truth. His footwork, he's getting through his progressions, his timing, his accuracy, the velocity he puts on the ball, the touch. And then when it's all said and done, the ability to create when it's not there." Purdy could be missing his top target on Sunday, though, as Mike Evans left the 49ers' last game before halftime due to injury. Atlanta's defense could get a key player of its own back for this one as A.J. Terrell Jr. began practicing this week after spending the last four games on injured reserve due to a groin injury. If both players suit up on Sunday, Terrell and Evans will rekindle a familiar matchup. Here's a look at who the experts predict will win on Sunday between the Falcons and 49ers. away.headline: 49ers injury updates: No major changes on 2nd week 7 practice report
away.blurb: There are a handful of players already ruled out for Week 7, but we could see some players back in action against the Falcons as the 49ers look to get a little healthier in time to go for a 7-0 start to the 2026 campaign. Christian Kirk trending toward return in Week 7 It's not a huge surprise to see optimism about Kirk's return for the 49ers' game in Atlanta. With Mike Evans potentially out because of Achilles tendinitis San Francisco needs reinforcements. Kirk's practice window was opened before Week 6, and now with a second week of practice in it sounds like the club is gearing up for him to come back in Week 7. Head coach Kyle Shanahan on Thursday spoke with KNBR and said Kirk is trending toward making his 2026 debut. " He looked good out there ," Shanahan said. "Talking to him he felt good, and I think he felt good last week. So it's trending in the right direction." The 49ers only open the first portion of practice to media, and neither Bosa nor Evans were on hand for the open part of the session according to reporters on site. Evans is working through Achilles tendonitis. He didn't practice leading up to Week 6 and still suited up before exiting the game late in the second quarter. For Bosa there was optimism he'd be back Thursday. Early indications are he isn't going to participate, but that could change if he comes out after media exit. Kyle Shanahan hopes Nick Bosa will return to practice Thursday Bosa has been out since Week 3 when he suffered a calf injury. The issue wasn't supposed be long-term and there was some hope he'd return for Week 6. Bosa didn't practice at all in Week 6 before being ruled out. He didn't participate in Wednesday's session, but head coach Kyle Shanahan expressed some optimism the star defensive end would be in the team's second practice of the week. "Can't go today, but hoping he'll be out there tomorrow," Shanahan said before practice. There may not be a team in the NFL more in need of a Bye week than the San Francisco 49ers . San Francisco will visit the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7, and then they'll be off for Week 8 where their injury situation could improve dramatically. We'll be keeping a close eye on the 49ers' injury updates all week. Follow along here: 49ers Thursday practice participation report Mike Evans, Nick Bosa not present for early part of Thursday practice Kyle Shanahan won't confirm Mike Evans injury severity There was a report from NFL Media's Ian Rapoport indicating the 49ers would have to manage Evans' Achilles tendonitis throughout the season. Shanahan would neither confirm nor deny that report while speaking with reporters ahead of Wednesday's practice. “We had to manage it last week and we're managing it this week," Shanahan said. "So, we'll see how the rest of the year goes.” It may behoove the 6-0 49ers to let their best pass rusher sit another week and then get the Bye before returning Week 9 at home vs. the Las Vegas Raiders. 49ers Wednesday practice participation report This article

picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI I'm all about celebrating a win, but the Tennessee Titans are coming up on a must-win game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. picks.headline: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7
picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. The total in this game currently sits at 37.5 over at FanDuel Sportsbook . That is the lowest total of the week, and the under might be the smart bet. The Titans are last in the league in yards per game at 236.3. The Browns are 29th at 267.5. Get ready for a lot of punts. The key for the Titans in this game will be taking care of the ball. Last week, the Titans forced three turnovers against the Indianapolis Colts. That, and a couple of key special teams plays, were the difference in the game. This game will likely play out in a similar way. Speaking of special teams plays, it was really good to see Chimere Dike break off a 58-yard punt return against the Colts. Dike was the biggest weapon the Titans had last season, but he had struggled this season before last week. Hopefully, that was the start of his return to the All-Pro returner he was last season. This game does feature two good rookie wide receivers. Denzel Boston leads all rookie receivers with 345 yards and is averaging over 20 yards per catch. Carnell Tate is right behind him with 344 yards. If one of those guys can break a big play, it could be the difference in this game. Don't expect a thrilling game when you sit down to watch this one on Sunday, but if the Titans can play a game similar to the one they did last week, they might have a chance at back-to-back wins for the first time since 2022.

away.headline: Browns Week 7 Injury Report Brings Mostly Good News for Titans Matchup
away.blurb: Ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Tennessee Titans , only two active players were officially ruled out for Cleveland in defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. and guard Teven Jenkins. Two others, DT Kalia Davis, as well as quarterback Dillon Gabriel were ruled out as well, but both remain on the IR for now. Meanwhile, a pretty star-heavy list of four players are listed as questionable for Sunday, starting with Grant Delpit, who has been in concussion protocol this week after exiting Sunday's win over the Ravens six plays into action with a head injury. He's been limited at practice in recent days as he works his way through the league's protocol. Running back Dillon Sampson is another, as is looking to return off the IR after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. He was limited throughout week, but could be activated to the active roster on Saturday and suit up on Sunday. Linebacker Quincy Williams was a late addition to the injury report this week after suffering a neck injury. He missed practice on Thursday, returned on Friday, but will still head into the weekend with a questionable designation. Similarly, cornerback Denzel Ward popped up on Friday's report with a hand injury and was limited at practice, promoting a questionable designation for him, as well. One such player is running back Quinshon Judkins, who will officially return this weekend after an ankle injury that kept him out of commission against the Baltimore Ravens last week. Additionally, DT Mason Graham will make a long awaited return, as well after missing each of the last two games with knee and ankle ailments. Graham actually returned to practice for the first time last Friday, but wasn't able to suit up in Week 6. The Ravens ruled out defensive tackle Broderick Washington Jr. (ankle), who didn't practice Thursday or Friday. He has six tackles so far this season. Minter also ruled out Cam Jurgens (concussion) for Sunday's game, meaning rookie Vega Ioane will get another start at center.. The Ravens also have other offensive line injuries to monitor with guards Andrew Vorhees (foot) and Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) both questionable to play. They were limited throughout the week. Wide receivers Zay Flowers (toe) and Rashod Bateman (shoulder) are good to go with no injury designation. Flowers was limited Thursday and Friday but Bateman returned to full participation. Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane could return from injured reserve after he suffered a wrist injury in Week 1 in Indianapolis. Lane had three full days of practice this week and is listed as questionable. He would have to be removed from injured reserve this weekend to play. While the Ravens could be at full strength at receiver, they're short at tight end with rookie Matt Hibner (hand) ruled out for Sunday's game. He didn't practice this week. Per Minter, the rookie tight end is not a candidate to be placed on injured reserve. The Vikings are 5-0 on the season and 4-1 against the spread, only failing to cover as -9.5 favorites in a 15-10 win over the Dolphins. On the other hand, the Colts fell to 2-4 last week with an upset loss to the previously winless Titans. It was their second straight loss after a 34-22 defeat in Pittsburgh on Oct. 11. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 7 matchup with a final score prediction. Heading into Week 7, they're 31st in net yards per play (-1.3), 21st in EPA per play, and 28th in opponent EPA per play. Their only redeeming quality has been Jonathan Taylor. If it wasn't for JT, their offensive numbers would be in the bottom five as well. If I close my eyes and think about this matchup, all I can envision is the Vikings' defense living in the Colts' backfield. Not only are they going to blitz Daniel Jones into oblivion, but they also lead the league in both opponent rush EPA and opponent rush success rate, meaning they're perfectly equipped to stop the one weapon Indianapolis has. The Vikings offense has me a bit concerned, but I'm hoping Kyler Murray can find some momentum after a BYE week. Pick: Vikings -5.5 (-118) via FanDuel This really is a horrible matchup for the Colts. Now, the Vikings may not be as strong as some undefeated teams of the past through five games, but they’ve still shown to be much better than the Vikings. And you can only beat who you’re scheduled to play. Minnesota deserves to be this big of a favorite out of its bye against the Colts. So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. So, Survivor players are going to have to at least consider a closer game to keep themselves alive. Here’s a quick recap of the Week 6 picks before we share our Week 7 selections. Week 7 may be the toughest week of the season, as some quality teams (Buffalo, Jacksonville mainly) are on the bye. Washington and the Los Angeles Chargers also won’t play in Week 7. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. They're fresh off a bye week and have arguably the best defense in the NFL. That very same defense is going to be able to put Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts' offense in a blender. It's clear by now that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, and the Vikings rank in the top three in virtually every single run defense stat. Kyler Murray should be able to produce enough offense to let his defense lead them to a win in this interconference duel. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.headline: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions as Kyle Murray & Co. Host the Colts in Week 7
picks.source: Minnesota Vikings On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: The Vikings will host a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday for just the third time this season as they welcome the 2-4 Colts to the Twin Cities in Week 7 . Minnesota looks to remain undefeated coming off an early Week 6 bye, while Indy will be scratching to salvage a start that has already led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard . Needless to say, these are two teams currently heading in completely different directions. With a beast of a November schedule looming, here are my predictions for a Vikings team looking to put together a dominating performance. 1. Kyler Murray will rack up 300-plus yards between the air and ground While the early bye provided desperately needed injury relief for the Vikings, there are fair concerns that the break may have disrupted the progress Kyler Murray and the passing game were starting to make. Murray’s performance in New Orleans was especially promising, mainly due to the fact that the offense entered the game without wideout Jordan Addison and left tackle Christian Darrisaw, and then lost tight end T.J. Hockenson to a concussion early. With all three looking to return this weekend, I see Murray having his best day yet in purple. Indy’s 351.2 yards allowed per game rank ninth in the league, and Murray’s abilities through the air and on the ground make him especially hard to stop (h/t: Ian Hartitz). After totaling 280 total yards against the Saints (229 passing, 51 rushing), I predict Murray will finish with over 300 total yards on Sunday. 2. Vikings' offense explodes for over 30 points The Vikings’ season started with a bang, scoring 39 points in the season opener against the Packers. Since then, they have not scored more than 23 points in a game. Sunday is the perfect opportunity for that to change. The Colts have given up 27.3 points per game so far this season, the sixth-highest average in the league. Minnesota, meanwhile, is looking for its first truly dominant offensive showing as it prepares for the hardest stretch of its schedule. The returns of Hockenson and Addison should open up passing options, and Jordan Mason’s possible return to the backfield could elevate a run game that Aaron Jones has carried almost entirely on his own so far. The Vikings’ offense needs to prove it can score consistently before facing some of the league's toughest opponents, and the Colts’ shaky defense may give them plenty of opportunities. 3. Harrison Smith wakes up and snags his 40th career interception Franchise legend Harrison Smith has had a relatively quiet start to his 15th NFL season . Smith announced his return a week before the Vikings kicked off their 2026 campaign and has mostly been a rotational piece in defensive coordinator Brian Flores’s ever-evolving defense. Even though “The Hitman” is clearly past his prime, he’s still one of the smartest defenders in the game, and I expect that to pay off this weekend. Smith recently confirmed to Richard Sherman that this will be his last season , so there is no better time to snag his 40th interception than now (h/t: "Richard Sherman Podcast"). Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has thrown six interceptions this season, tied for the third-most in the league , and anyone who's watched him through his career knows he’ll eventually throw a duck or two (h/t: NFL). Smith’s football IQ and Jones’s occasional recklessness may just be the perfect combination to get the NFL’s active interception leader his next pick. With Shane Steichen in the hot seat after a rough 2-4 start, the Indianapolis Colts are teetering on the brink of a lost season, and they're 6.5-point underdogs for Sunday's visit to the unbeaten Minnesota Vikings. Fresh off a bye week, Minnesota leads an ultra-competitive NFC North, and my Colts vs Vikings predictions point to the hosts' aggressive defense sparking another comfortable win at U.S. Bank Stadium. My NFL picks dig into this Sunday Oct. 25 battle, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET on CBS. TOP Pick Colts vs Vikings prediction: Vikings -6.5 This ruthless Minnesota Vikings start is no fluke – they've won 10 straight games dating back to last season, with an 8-2 ATS mark in that span , and their blitzing defense has Daniel Jones in its sights on Sunday. Brian Flores' aggressive unit ranks among the stingiest in the league against both the pass and the run (just 259.8 YPG allowed overall), and that spells trouble for an Indianapolis Colts team that's lost 11 of its past 13 contests and had three costly turnovers last weekend. Minnesota's bye week has also cleaned up the injury report, with T.J. Hockenson , Jordan Addison, and Jordan Mason returning to diversify an offense that racked up 364 yards in Week 5 and capitalized on the defense's forced field position . Meanwhile, Indy is unlikely to have Sauce Gardner to throw at the Justin Jefferson assignment and could also be without key target Tyler Warren . Jones has already turned the ball over nine times through the first six games , and I'd bet this to 53%. Colts vs Vikings combo I expect a Minnesota win to come with a sharper offensive outing, with an extra week of preparation and more weapons for Kyler Murray to call on. The Vikings scored 39 points in their home opener against Green Bay, while the Colts gave up at least 30 points in road losses to Pittsburgh and Kansas City. The Over has been a winning ticket in Indy's last two contests, and this line feels too low for a matchup featuring Jefferson and (possible trade candidate) Jonathan Taylor on an indoor track. Jones' brief spell with the Vikings in 2024 at least means he knows what to expect here. Expect the Indy offense to lean heavily on Taylor and quick checkdowns. That's where Keenan Allen can thrive on Sunday, and he's been busy in his last three appearances, catching 19 of 29 targets for 190 yards . The Minnesota blitz will limit Jones's deep shots, but Allen's ability to win on short routes is highly valuable in this matchup. Vikings moneyline Keenan Allen Over 39.5 receiving yards Colts vs Vikings touchdown scorer: Justin Jefferson This is a great price on a Jefferson touchdown, especially with Gardner expected to be sidelined and the Colts' secondary overmatched. The Vikings' No.1 receiver already has three scores this season, and he shouldn't be tied down by as many double teams with Addison and Hockenson back this weekend. Jefferson had two TDs in the season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium, and this is a favorable matchup against an Indy defense that gave up six passing touchdowns in road losses to Patrick Mahomes and Aaron Rodgers. picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:55 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings enter their Week 7 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts looking to extend the league's longest winning streak. Since Week 14 of the 2025 season, the Vikings have won 10 straight games, building a 5-0 record going into last week's bye. They face a 2-4 Indianapolis team that fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Head coach Shane Steichen is still employed , but the Colts feel combustible right now, with rumors of trading away star players like RB Jonathan Taylor and G Quenton Nelson swirling. Minnesota can't afford to overlook Indianapolis if they want to keep pace with the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. But this feels like an opportunity for the Vikings to jump on an inferior team that is going through organizational changes. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings when they host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday. Jordan Mason will run for 100+ yards and 2 touchdowns Jordan Mason appears to return to the lineup after missing the past four games with a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen on Tuesday that he expects to see Mason, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Christian Darrisaw back at practice on Wednesday . With Mason back, Minnesota can return to its 1-2 punch with Aaron Jones. Indianapolis enters Week 7 as one of the league's worst run defenses. They rank 22nd in rushing yards allowed, but their 4.8 yards per run allowed is tied for 5th-worst in the league. Their 12.3% stuff-rate ranks 30th in the league, and they rank last in EPA/run allowed. I expect the Vikings to stay committed to the run game and give Jones some relief after he carried the ball 85 times for 370 yards from Weeks 2 to 5. Mason averaged 3.5 yards after contact per carry in 2025, tied for 11th-best in the league among qualifying running backs. I see him breaking 100 yards and reaching the end zone twice on Sunday. Jauan Jennings will catch a touchdown pass Trade rumors swirled around Jauan Jennings in the days after Minnesota's 23-13 win over the Saints in Week 5. He was caught on camera slamming his fist into the ground following Myles Price's fumble that was returned for a touchdown. That came two plays after Jennings appeared to get open for a potential touchdown, but Murray instead threw an incompletion to Tai Felton. One play later, Murray slightly overthrew Jennings in the end zone. Jennings has caught only two passes for nine yards this season, but the rumors of a potential trade seem to have died down. He's gotten open enough that he should be getting more targets, but look for him to find more separation downfield, with Justin Jefferson, Addison, and Hockenson potentially back this week. With extra attention on the other weapons on the field, Murray will make up for his red zone misses against the Saints. The Vikings will sack Daniel Jones 5+ times and pick him off multiple times This will be the first time Daniel Jones plays against the Vikings since spending the end of the 2024 season with them. He signed with the Colts last year and played well until a fractured fibula in Week 12 slowed him down, and an Achilles tear ended his season two weeks later. He completed 68% of his passes for 3,101 yards (8.1 yards per attempt), 19 touchdowns, and eight interceptions. Jones hasn't been as efficient this season, completing 59.6% of his passes and averaging 5.9 yards per attempt, with four touchdowns and six picks. He has been pressured on 42.1% of his dropbacks, tied for the league's 7th-highest mark. Of course, no one pressures quarterbacks as much as Minnesota does. They have a league-high 47.8% quarterback pressure rate, spearheaded by a 67.0% blitz rate that is 24.5 percentage points higher than the next-closest team. Look for the Vikings to get after Jones all day and force him into turnovers. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7

away.headline: Final injury report: Jordan Mason questionable, Colts down two key starters
away.blurb: Coming out of their bye week, the Vikings have almost a perfectly clean injury report as they head into the weekend preparing to host the Colts on Sunday at U.S. Bank Stadium. After everyone on the 53-man roster was a full participant in Thursday’s practice, the Vikings do not have any players on their active roster with game designations on Friday. The only player listed as questionable is running back Jordan Mason, who practiced in full all week and is expected to make his return on Sunday after missing the past four games with a thumb injury. “Jordan Mason practiced fully all week,” Kevin O’Connell said. “Really good week of work. We’ll work through what that looks like, but he is technically questionable right now. Things are looking positive for him being available.” It sounds like Mason is essentially only listed as questionable because he’s still on injured reserve at the moment. He’ll almost certainly be activated from IR on Saturday, which will require a corresponding roster move. Mason and Aaron Jones are expected to split carries in Minnesota’s backfield moving forward. Wide receiver Jordan Addison, left tackle Christian Darrisaw, and tight end T.J. Hockenson will also be back in action after missing the Vikings’ most recent game in New Orleans prior to the bye. The Vikings have had Kyler Murray, Justin Jefferson, and Addison on the field together for a total of 18 snaps this season. That’s about to change, which is good news for an offense that hasn’t been great for much of the first five weeks. The 2-4 Colts will be without a key starter on both sides of the ball in this one. Tight end Tyler Warren, who leads the team with 30 receptions, will miss a second consecutive game with a groin injury. That’s a big blow for Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis offense. Defensively, the Colts will be without top cornerback Sauce Gardner due to a calf injury. Charvarius Ward and Cam Taylor-Britt are the Colts’ top healthy outside cornerbacks. It’s a 12 p.m. kickoff on Sunday on CBS. away.headline: Colts key playmaker remains sidelined with injury
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. Related Articles Bears React to NFL Announcement for QB Caleb Williams Following His Return According to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk, Colts second-year tight end Tyler Warren was still sidelined on Wednesday with a groin injury. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns. He won Super Bowl XLIV with New Orleans. Morstead was originally selected by the Saints in the fifth round (164th overall) of the 2009 NFL Draft out of SMU. In 2012, he was an Associated Press Second Team All-Pro choice and was named to the Pro Bowl. Pancol, 6-3, 205 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on September 23, 2026. The Jets are early 4.5-point favorites, but the Dolphins' improving rushing attack creates room for several bold predictions. Ollie Gordon II will rush for at least 100 yards. Gordon has totaled 188 yards in two starts since De'Von Achane went on injured reserve. Miami's 217-yard performance against Cincinnati should convince the coaching staff to keep the offense on the ground. New York has been much stronger against the pass than the run, which gives Gordon a favorable path to volume. Malik Willis will produce two touchdowns and no more than one turnover. This is the prediction that would change the game. Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble against Cincinnati, but the bye gives Miami time to reduce his difficult reads. Designed runs and play-action can turn his mobility into production while limiting risky throws. Miami will record at least three sacks. The Dolphins have only four sacks through five games, making this the boldest defensive call. Hafley's staff has two weeks to design pressure packages against Geno Smith.
