away.headline: Dolphins' Jeff Hafley returns to New Jersey seeking first Miami win
away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley likes to say it's about the team and not about him, but he sure would like to have his first NFL head-coaching win take place in his home state of New Jersey. "My mom will be there," Hafley said of a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . "I'll have a lot of people there. My brother, my sister, I'll probably have 30-plus people at the game. For all of us, I think it's always nice to go back close to home." Hafley hails from Montvale, N.J., only 17 miles from MetLife Stadium where Sunday's game will be played. The Dolphins are 0-5 but entered the week only 4.5-point underdogs at the Jets , who are 2-4. More Jeff Hafley: Jeff Hafley, Bruce Springsteen connected by more than New Jersey Miami's first five opponents were NFL playoff contenders. The Jets likely are not. And here is more good news: the Dolphins are coming off of an early bye week. "New energy, man," said Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks. "Just a chance to reset. Wasn't a friendly first five weeks of the season. It was tough, kind of going through that. And we still got to live with it, but I think that break gives you a chance to kind of reflect and kind of take a deep breath and I think that's what this team needed." Predictably, the Dolphins' statistical resume after five games is poor. Miami ranks better than the league average in only 8 of the top 32 essential categories sorted and ranked by the NFL. What have the Dolphins done fairly well? "Right now, we're a team that's running the ball very well, and we're playing pretty good run defense, too," Hafley said. "We're a physical team. I think we have to build on that identity and continue to grow and develop." Miami Dolphins seek development, but also a win A lot of growth, development and patience will be required. Coaches often say they use the bye week to "self-scout" in an attempt to improve in areas they may have overlooked in the day-to-day grind of a game week. "With such a small sample size, it's not huge, but a really good time to evaluate and catch your breath and sometimes when you get to step back, you can see some things clearly," Hafley said. There are many areas in which the Dolphins must improve to win a game (short-term goal) and finish better than, say, 2-15 or 3-14 this season. But here are some self-scout reflections Dolphins players have spoken about after the bye. Malik Willis wants fewer turnovers Quarterback Malik Willis has 4 interceptions and 5 fumbles in his first 5 games with the team. He was listed on the Injury Report with an injured right thumb, but has been practicing all week and will start. "It just can't happen, you know?" Willis said. "I mean, regardless of what went down to force the turnovers, you just can't have them, regardless. And just risk management because there's no fault, it's just the turnover goes to me, so it doesn't matter. It’s on me." away.headline: Miami Dolphins injury report: Rookie WR Caleb Douglas back for Jets
away.blurb: Douglas had been out since Week 2 when he suffered a sprained ankle against the San Francisco 49ers. Despite missing the last three games for 0-5 Miami, Douglas leads the Dolphins with 56.5 reception yards per game. The Jets likely will be missing LB Kiko Mauigo (quad), OL Max Mitchel (concussion), RB Kene Nwangwu (knee) and EDGE Joseph Ossai (ankle), who all did not practice on Thursday. "Caleb will play," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said at his Friday press conference. Linebacker Willie Gay was ill and missed Thursday's practice. Hafley said he was feeling better on Friday morning and was expected to be at practice. Meanwhile, quarterback Malik Willis, who did not throw during the bye week with an injured right thumb, has been practicing and is good to go. Hafley said running back Jaylen Wright (foot) will play. Tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring) said Thursday that he's good to go. Promising rookie safety/linebacker Kyle Louis has been on the Physically Unable to Perform list since injuring his knee in the season-opener at Las Vegas. Hafley said he wants to wait until Friday's practice to determine if Louis will be activated. "He has stayed sharp but you're talking about a rookie who hasn't played much football," he said. One new face Dolphins fans will see Sunday is placekicker Zane Gonzalez. Hafley talked about Gonzalez replacing Riley Patterson as the team's placekicker earlier in the week. He said it wasn't meant as a message. "We felt it was best for our team going forward," Hafley said. "Zane did a great job when he was here and then he was injured." away.blurb: Miami’s only Wednesday nonparticipant was cornerback Reese Taylor, who continues to deal with a quadriceps injury. Long snapper Tucker Addington, edge rusher Rob Beal Jr., receiver Caleb Douglas, tight end Will Kacmarek, safety Kyle Louis and running back Jaylen Wright were limited. The Jets held Hall out Wednesday because of a quadriceps injury. Kene Nwangwu missed practice with a knee problem, increasing the potential importance of Allen. Linebacker Kiko Mauigoa and edge rusher Joseph Ossai also did not participate because of quadriceps and ankle injuries. Veteran linebacker Demario Davis and defensive lineman Harrison Phillips received rest days. Receiver Adonai Mitchell, guard Dylan Parham, edge rusher Will McDonald IV and defensive lineman T’Vondre Sweat were limited. Parham’s knee affects New York’s interior protection, while McDonald and Ossai influence a pass rush built to attack Miami’s protection. No game-status designations were assigned Wednesday. Thursday’s progression matters: players moving from limited to full are trending toward availability, while a second missed practice would raise concern. Friday’s report will provide the official out, doubtful and questionable labels. Miami opened Jets week with encouraging news at quarterback, right guard and cornerback. New York began with greater uncertainty in its backfield and edge rotation. Quarterback Malik Willis was listed with a right thumb injury but practiced fully Wednesday. His participation indicates the injury did not prevent him from handling the complete workload. Willis remains expected to start Sunday. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea also practiced fully after an ankle injury forced him from the Cincinnati game. That is an important development against a Jets defense with 17 sacks. Jarrett Kingston remains an experienced contingency, but a full practice puts Savaiinaea on track to reclaim his starting position. Cornerback JuJu Brents , listed with a heel injury, was a full participant. Linebackers Jordyn Brooks and Jackson Woodard also practiced fully despite foot and ankle issues. Their progress strengthens a defense preparing for Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr. and a Jets rushing attack that may again rely on Braelon Allen. He has seven catches for 113 yards in two games and would add a vertical element to a passing attack averaging only two touchdowns through five games. away.headline: Caleb Douglas could return to Miami Dolphins lineup against New York Jets
away.blurb: “Caleb will be limited [in practice] today. You know, we’ll see how he looks today and progress to Wednesday, but I think there’s optimism there. Let’s see how it goes today, and if he can get ramped up on Wednesday, it would be good to get him back out there.” The Miami Dolphins had a much needed bye week this past weekend. Multiple players have been banged up, including standout rookie receiver Caleb Douglas. It seems the added rest has been a good thing for the young pass catcher, as according to head coach Jeff Hafley, Douglas has a chance to suit up against the New York Jets on the road this upcoming Sunday. During his press availability on Monday morning, head coach Jeff Hafley was asked about Douglas’ potential to practice this week. Hafley, with a smile on his face, would go on to speak about what Miami missed on offense without Douglas in the mix. “Just kind of looking back through the last couple of weeks, some of the things that he did, we’ve missed him. And to see a rookie kind of have to start and stop like that, not ideal. But, he’s worked really hard and it would be very great to get him back.” We will keep a close eye on Douglas’ practice participation as the week unfolds, but as of Monday afternoon, his availability seems to be pointing in a positive direction in regards to playing this Sunday.

home.headline: Jets vs. Dolphins live injury updates: Full Wednesday news from Aaron Glenn
home.blurb: As is always the case in the NFL, the injury report will be watched throughout the coming days until kickoff. Ahead of the Sunday game scheduled for 1 p.m. at MetLife Stadium, the Jets (2-4) have a few names that will be watched. Some of the top ones include running back Breece Hall ( quad ) wide receiver AD Mitchell (finger) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). Will those injured Jets players and others be healthy enough to suit up against the Dolphins (0-5)? Stay tuned right here with Jets Wire's running list of injury updates from practices throughout the coming days:

home.headline: Miami Dolphins injury report: Rookie WR Caleb Douglas back for Jets
home.blurb: Douglas had been out since Week 2 when he suffered a sprained ankle against the San Francisco 49ers. Despite missing the last three games for 0-5 Miami, Douglas leads the Dolphins with 56.5 reception yards per game. The Jets likely will be missing LB Kiko Mauigo (quad), OL Max Mitchel (concussion), RB Kene Nwangwu (knee) and EDGE Joseph Ossai (ankle), who all did not practice on Thursday. "Caleb will play," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said at his Friday press conference. Linebacker Willie Gay was ill and missed Thursday's practice. Hafley said he was feeling better on Friday morning and was expected to be at practice. Meanwhile, quarterback Malik Willis, who did not throw during the bye week with an injured right thumb, has been practicing and is good to go. Hafley said running back Jaylen Wright (foot) will play. Tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring) said Thursday that he's good to go. Promising rookie safety/linebacker Kyle Louis has been on the Physically Unable to Perform list since injuring his knee in the season-opener at Las Vegas. Hafley said he wants to wait until Friday's practice to determine if Louis will be activated. "He has stayed sharp but you're talking about a rookie who hasn't played much football," he said. One new face Dolphins fans will see Sunday is placekicker Zane Gonzalez. Hafley talked about Gonzalez replacing Riley Patterson as the team's placekicker earlier in the week. He said it wasn't meant as a message. "We felt it was best for our team going forward," Hafley said. "Zane did a great job when he was here and then he was injured." home.headline: Miami Dolphins-New York Jets Injury Report: Willis and Savaiinaea Full, Hall Sits
home.blurb: Miami’s only Wednesday nonparticipant was cornerback Reese Taylor, who continues to deal with a quadriceps injury. Long snapper Tucker Addington, edge rusher Rob Beal Jr., receiver Caleb Douglas, tight end Will Kacmarek, safety Kyle Louis and running back Jaylen Wright were limited. The Jets held Hall out Wednesday because of a quadriceps injury. Kene Nwangwu missed practice with a knee problem, increasing the potential importance of Allen. Linebacker Kiko Mauigoa and edge rusher Joseph Ossai also did not participate because of quadriceps and ankle injuries. Veteran linebacker Demario Davis and defensive lineman Harrison Phillips received rest days. Receiver Adonai Mitchell, guard Dylan Parham, edge rusher Will McDonald IV and defensive lineman T’Vondre Sweat were limited. Parham’s knee affects New York’s interior protection, while McDonald and Ossai influence a pass rush built to attack Miami’s protection. No game-status designations were assigned Wednesday. Thursday’s progression matters: players moving from limited to full are trending toward availability, while a second missed practice would raise concern. Friday’s report will provide the official out, doubtful and questionable labels. Miami opened Jets week with encouraging news at quarterback, right guard and cornerback. New York began with greater uncertainty in its backfield and edge rotation. Quarterback Malik Willis was listed with a right thumb injury but practiced fully Wednesday. His participation indicates the injury did not prevent him from handling the complete workload. Willis remains expected to start Sunday. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea also practiced fully after an ankle injury forced him from the Cincinnati game. That is an important development against a Jets defense with 17 sacks. Jarrett Kingston remains an experienced contingency, but a full practice puts Savaiinaea on track to reclaim his starting position. Cornerback JuJu Brents , listed with a heel injury, was a full participant. Linebackers Jordyn Brooks and Jackson Woodard also practiced fully despite foot and ankle issues. Their progress strengthens a defense preparing for Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr. and a Jets rushing attack that may again rely on Braelon Allen. Walking Wounded Still Limping About Douglas’ ankle remains one of the more significant offensive questions. He has seven catches for 113 yards in two games and would add a vertical element to a passing attack averaging only two touchdowns through five games. Wright’s foot and Kacmarek’s hamstring also affect the depth behind Gordon and Dulcich.

home.headline: New York Jets Have a Lot of Mystery on Injury List
home.blurb: The Jets have three players out, two defensive players listed as limited in practice, and three limited for the offense. That’s including three players definitively out for the Miami game. So far, running back Breece Hall is the biggest mystery. He’s recovering from a quad injury sustained during the Detroit game in Week 3 and is just back at practice, though limited, and was kept out of Wednesday’s practice. He’s looking doubtful for Sunday, particularly with backup Braelon Allen doing a huge job as the fill-in. Officially out for Sunday’s game are linebacker Kiko Mauigoa, edge rusher Joseph Ossai, and offensive lineman Max Mitchell, who will not play because of a concussion. The first two have been frequent flyers on the Jets injury list this season, while Mitchell is a valued backup. Starting left guard Dylan Parham was listed as questionable on the Jets injury report after practicing on a limited basis. Jordan Meredith has been the fill-in, but is not nearly at Parham’s level. Another potential problem for the Jets is in the return game. Gamebreaker Kene Nwangwu did not practice and is nursing a knee injury, not a great sign for someone who relies on speed. Nwangwu sustained several big hits on returns in the New England game and has generally struggled to break off a long one this year for the Jets special teams. Long-lost receiver Adonai Mitchell is expected to return to action on Sunday. He’s been out with a murky diagnosis of a finger injury that first didn’t need a medical intervention, then did. Now it’s a matter of pain tolerance for the receiver, according to head coach Aaron Glenn. If Mitchell plays, it will be the first time since opening day that the Jets have their three top receivers – Mitchell, Garrett Wilson, and Omar Cooper Jr. – available in the same game. Mitchell was establishing himself as a solid No. 2 option prior to his injury, and Cooper just won the NFL Rookie of the Week honors for his solid performance against New England. Either or both can offer to draw some attention away from Wilson, opening things up for the moribund Jets offense. Left guard Dylan Parham is listed as questionable for Sunday with a lingering knee injury. He played well before going down, but it remains uncertain how much the knee will limit his mobility. The New York Jets have a lot of questions, particularly about who will line up against the winless Miami Dolphins for Sunday’s game. Hall created intrigue by posting an Instagram of himself that said “Soon” earlier this week. Whether that translates to this Sunday remains to be seen. The 2-4 Jets are home against winless Miami on Sunday at MetLife Stadium. The early line has the Jets as 5.5 point favorites, not an overwhelming spread.

home.headline: Baker Mayfield set to start for Bucs' Week 7 game vs. Panthers; WR Emeka Egbuka ruled out with concussion
home.blurb: Baker Mayfield set to start for Bucs' Week 7 game vs. Panthers; WR Emeka Egbuka ruled out with concussion - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL In this story Baker Mayfield is set to make his return Sunday in Carolina, according to Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles, who told reporters Friday that his two-time Pro Bowl quarterback looks "ready to go" for the road game versus the Panthers. Although Mayfield is technically listed as "questionable" on the Bucs' injury report , he was a full participant in practice all week . His expected return will mark his first game since Sept. 27. Back then, during a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, Mayfield dislocated the thumb on his throwing hand . Mayfield's three-week recovery timeline was reportedly the best-case scenario. Even though Mayfield is re-entering the lineup, he won't have one of his top wideouts to throw to, as Tampa Bay ruled out Emeka Egbuka on Friday. Egbuka's been in concussion protocol this week. Bowles said Friday, via Laine , that the Bucs couldn't figure out which play Egbuka suffered the concussion. Notably, Egbuka absorbed a fourth-quarter blow from Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen, whose shoulder collided with Egbuka's helmet on an incomplete pass. F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on Andy Backstrom Contributing writer Fri, October 23, 2026 at 6:31 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Egbuka didn't leave last week's overtime defeat to the Pittsburgh Steelers with the injury. It wasn't until he was back in facility this week that his symptoms surfaced, leading to him being placed in the protocol, as reported by ESPN's Jenna Laine . But Bowles said Friday that "there were several plays that it could have happened or not happened on." Egbuka, who's also dealing with a foot issue, currently leads the 1-5 Buccaneers with 28 receptions and 240 receiving yards. The second-year pro also has a team-high two touchdown grabs. In addition to missing Egbuka, Tampa Bay will be down right tackle Luke Goedeke. He'll be sidelined with a calf injury that he picked up last week. Despite those absences, Mayfield will have to deliver a much-needed win against the NFC South rival Panthers. In Mayfield's place, the Bucs turned to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. He went 1-2 in his three starts, highlighted by a "Thursday Night Football" win over the Dallas Cowboys. But the Kansas product has posted a meager 3:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio over four appearances, with two of those picks coming last week against the Steelers. Daniels threw a pair of fourth-quarter interceptions, and Tampa Bay blew a 13-point lead in the final frame .

home.headline: Panthers HC Dave Canales provides encouraging updates on CBs Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson
home.blurb: Head coach Dave Canales spoke with reporters following this afternoon's practice, just ahead of their upcoming bout against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . He was asked about the progress of corners Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, who have been on injured reserve for the past few weeks. "Jaycee is doing great," Canales stated. "The reports I get are that he's trending in the right direction—ahead of whatever general deadlines. He's crushing his rehab right now. He's itching to just keep taking the next step. "Mike Jack, same thing. He's moving around, they're starting to pick up their speeds, the change-of-direction stuff. Those are all the things, with the nature of the injuries that have to feel really good before you're able to open up. Obviously, we gotta go through the four games. And then, after that, you start thinking about opening up windows." Both Horn (quad) and Jackson (groin) went down during the team's Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns . Initial reports suggested that Horn would be in danger of missing the remainder of the campaign while Jackson was expected back some time in November. Carolina, in their places, have started rookie Will Lee III and special teams ace Akayleb Evans. Follow @ThePanthersWire on Twitter/X for more Panthers content. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. Lamar Jackson (ankle) seen walking off practice field with a limp, per @CordellWoodland . https://t.co/1R708hsFHo That's a sign that Jackson isn't expected to play in Week 7, and he may need to log a full practice on Thursday or Friday to shift the sentiment in the betting market. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers this week about how they set the line for a game like this with Jackson's status up in the air. "Your lookahead line, you essentially have to assume he's going to play until you hear otherwise.," Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. "So, that's baked into the price, whether we anticipate he'll be at full strength or 80% strength, that would kind of be factored in there. "And then, as the week goes on, we'll adjust as we know more. Obviously, he wasn't at practice today, and our line went down a point and a half just off that alone. And then we'll kind of trickle down as the week goes on and his status becomes more and more certain one way or the other. If he's back at practice tomorrow in a limited or full capacity, the line will probably shift back towards the Ravens. If he's not there again on Thursday, we'll essentially start pricing as though [Tyler] Huntley is going to be the starter." So, what could the line close at if Huntley makes his third start in a row? "If he's out and it's Huntley again, the line will most likely shift to the Bengals being the favorite, probably in that 1.5 to 2.5 range," Gour said. So, based on Gour's projection, the current line suggest that Jackson won't play. That would be a huge blow to a Ravens team that is 4-2 and already lost a division game in Week 6. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score while leading the NFL in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating. The Ravens are 7-12 all time without Jackson, though they've won three of the four starts Huntley has made in his place since the 2025 season. Bettors are going to want to monitor Baltimore's practice report on Thursday, as it could solidify Jackson's status for Sunday's game. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. away.headline: Lamar Jackson Reveals Severity of Ankle Injury, Latest on QB's Status for Ravens vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Jackson had gone through "a good couple of days" since rejoining practice in a limited capacity this week for the first time since Week 4. The ankle injury forced Jackson to miss the last two games, and Baltimore has gone 1-1 during that stretch. He reportedly had a chance to play in the Ravens' Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, but ultimately wasn't ready to return as Baltimore lost 13-10. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson says he is "heading in the right direction" and could play in Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after returning to practice earlier this week. "I can't call it right now. Still got a grace period. We'll see, man. Hopefully," Jackson said Friday. "But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now." "It's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective... he feels like he can be," Minter said (h/t ESPN's Jamison Hensley). After avoiding injuries through the first three games of the season, Jackson exited the Ravens' Week 4 game against the Tennessee Titans due to an ankle injury. In four games, Jackson has thrown for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, adding 144 yards and a score on the ground. The Ravens are sitting at 4-2 on the season heading into this week's matchup against the Bengals. Tyler Huntley has filled in for Jackson in his absence and has collected 429 passing yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions. Injuries have unfortunately been the story for Jackson over the last two seasons. He missed four games last year and finished the 2025 campaign with 2,549 passing yards, 21 touchdowns and seven interceptions, while rushing for 349 yards and two touchdowns. The Ravens finished the season 8-9 and missed the playoffs, and they're hoping to avoid a repeat of the 2025 campaign.

away.headline: Ravens rule out Jaylinn Hawkins with knee injury ahead of Bengals
away.blurb: The Ravens will face Cincinnati’s passing attack without safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who has been ruled out for Sunday’s game with a knee injury. Coach Jesse Minter indicated Friday that the injury is not expected to be a long-term issue but did not provide a specific return timetable, according to Brian Wacker. Hawkins has appeared in all six games this season, making three starts and recording 30 tackles, including 17 solo stops. He matched his season high with eight tackles in Sunday’s 13-10 loss at Cleveland. His absence requires another adjustment for a secondary preparing to defend Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Cincinnati arrives after its bye, while Baltimore tries to recover from its first division loss. Kyle Hamilton and Malaki Starks remain central to the Ravens’ safety options. How Baltimore replaces Hawkins’ snaps could also influence Hamilton’s deployment, given his responsibilities near the line of scrimmage and in coverage. Hamilton has played 33% of his snaps in the slot, 33% at linebacker and 20% at safety, according to Next Gen Stats figures cited by Cincinnati’s official scouting report. That versatility gives Baltimore flexibility, but replacing Hawkins still requires balancing its coverage and run-defense assignments. The Ravens also learned Friday that outside linebacker Tavius Robinson will miss the remainder of the season with a pectoral injury. Hawkins’ outlook appears less severe, but his immediate absence leaves Baltimore replacing contributors at two levels of its defense against a rested division rival.

away.headline: Ravens leave Bengals guessing if Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley will start Week 7 game
away.blurb: It was widely assumed that Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter would announce on Friday afternoon that either first-choice option Lamar Jackson or backup Tyler Huntley would start at quarterback for this coming Sunday's game between the 4-2 Ravens and 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium. Minter instead went in a different direction while speaking with reporters. Lamar Jackson, Ravens "still working through" his status for Bengals game "We're still working through that," Minter said about Jackson's availability for the Bengals game, as shared by the Ravens ' X (formerly Twitter) account. "He's been able to get some work in these last couple of days." Jackson has not played since he suffered an ankle injury in the Ravens' 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. While Huntley helped Baltimore earn a 30-23 overtime victory at the Atlanta Falcons back on Oct. 11, he later completed 19-of-31 passes for 165 yards and one touchdown in the Ravens' 13-10 loss at the rival Cleveland Browns on Oct. 18. Lamar Jackson shares specifics about ankle injury A previous report said that Jackson's ankle issue was "unconventional" and wasn't considered a high-ankle sprain or a low-ankle sprain. Per Jamison Hensley of ESPN, Jackson confirmed on Friday afternoon that he is dealing with a high-ankle sprain. Jackson also insisted that he doesn't need to be considered fully healthy to face the Bengals' defense. "Right now, I’m heading in the right direction," Jackson said about playing against the Bengals. He added that "hopefully" he will be good to go by Sunday morning. While Jackson revealed that the swelling in the ankle has gone down significantly, he also hinted that he's still dealing with quite a bit of discomfort related to the initial injury. That comment could lead one to believe that the Ravens may wait until Saturday or even Sunday to announce their QB1 for the Bengals game. Shortly after Jackson spoke, DraftKings Sportsbook had the Ravens as 1.5-point home favorites over the Bengals. It remains to be seen how that line will move, if at all, once outsiders learn whether Jackson or Huntley will be in the Baltimore lineup. Want more articles like this? Huntley completed 19-of-31 passes for 165 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions against Cleveland. He also had 28 rushing yards on five carries, and was sacked three times. Huntley has started 13 games over six seasons with the Ravens. He has not started a regular-season game against Cincinnati, but did start for the Ravens in their 24-17 postseason loss to Cincinnati in Jan. 2023. home.headline: Lamar Jackson Reveals Severity of Ankle Injury, Latest on QB's Status for Ravens vs. Bengals
home.blurb: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Jackson had gone through "a good couple of days" since rejoining practice in a limited capacity this week for the first time since Week 4. The ankle injury forced Jackson to miss the last two games, and Baltimore has gone 1-1 during that stretch. He reportedly had a chance to play in the Ravens' Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, but ultimately wasn't ready to return as Baltimore lost 13-10. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson says he is "heading in the right direction" and could play in Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after returning to practice earlier this week. "I can't call it right now. Still got a grace period. We'll see, man. Hopefully," Jackson said Friday. "But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now." "It's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective... he feels like he can be," Minter said (h/t ESPN's Jamison Hensley). After avoiding injuries through the first three games of the season, Jackson exited the Ravens' Week 4 game against the Tennessee Titans due to an ankle injury. In four games, Jackson has thrown for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, adding 144 yards and a score on the ground. The Ravens are sitting at 4-2 on the season heading into this week's matchup against the Bengals. Tyler Huntley has filled in for Jackson in his absence and has collected 429 passing yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions. Injuries have unfortunately been the story for Jackson over the last two seasons. He missed four games last year and finished the 2025 campaign with 2,549 passing yards, 21 touchdowns and seven interceptions, while rushing for 349 yards and two touchdowns. The Ravens finished the season 8-9 and missed the playoffs, and they're hoping to avoid a repeat of the 2025 campaign.

home.headline: Ravens rule out Jaylinn Hawkins with knee injury ahead of Bengals
home.blurb: The Ravens will face Cincinnati’s passing attack without safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who has been ruled out for Sunday’s game with a knee injury. Coach Jesse Minter indicated Friday that the injury is not expected to be a long-term issue but did not provide a specific return timetable, according to Brian Wacker. Hawkins has appeared in all six games this season, making three starts and recording 30 tackles, including 17 solo stops. He matched his season high with eight tackles in Sunday’s 13-10 loss at Cleveland. His absence requires another adjustment for a secondary preparing to defend Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Cincinnati arrives after its bye, while Baltimore tries to recover from its first division loss. Kyle Hamilton and Malaki Starks remain central to the Ravens’ safety options. How Baltimore replaces Hawkins’ snaps could also influence Hamilton’s deployment, given his responsibilities near the line of scrimmage and in coverage. Hamilton has played 33% of his snaps in the slot, 33% at linebacker and 20% at safety, according to Next Gen Stats figures cited by Cincinnati’s official scouting report. That versatility gives Baltimore flexibility, but replacing Hawkins still requires balancing its coverage and run-defense assignments. The Ravens also learned Friday that outside linebacker Tavius Robinson will miss the remainder of the season with a pectoral injury. Hawkins’ outlook appears less severe, but his immediate absence leaves Baltimore replacing contributors at two levels of its defense against a rested division rival.

home.headline: Ravens leave Bengals guessing if Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley will start Week 7 game
home.blurb: It was widely assumed that Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter would announce on Friday afternoon that either first-choice option Lamar Jackson or backup Tyler Huntley would start at quarterback for this coming Sunday's game between the 4-2 Ravens and 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium. Minter instead went in a different direction while speaking with reporters. Lamar Jackson, Ravens "still working through" his status for Bengals game "We're still working through that," Minter said about Jackson's availability for the Bengals game, as shared by the Ravens ' X (formerly Twitter) account. "He's been able to get some work in these last couple of days." Jackson has not played since he suffered an ankle injury in the Ravens' 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. While Huntley helped Baltimore earn a 30-23 overtime victory at the Atlanta Falcons back on Oct. 11, he later completed 19-of-31 passes for 165 yards and one touchdown in the Ravens' 13-10 loss at the rival Cleveland Browns on Oct. 18. Lamar Jackson shares specifics about ankle injury A previous report said that Jackson's ankle issue was "unconventional" and wasn't considered a high-ankle sprain or a low-ankle sprain. Per Jamison Hensley of ESPN, Jackson confirmed on Friday afternoon that he is dealing with a high-ankle sprain. Jackson also insisted that he doesn't need to be considered fully healthy to face the Bengals' defense. "Right now, I’m heading in the right direction," Jackson said about playing against the Bengals. He added that "hopefully" he will be good to go by Sunday morning. While Jackson revealed that the swelling in the ankle has gone down significantly, he also hinted that he's still dealing with quite a bit of discomfort related to the initial injury. That comment could lead one to believe that the Ravens may wait until Saturday or even Sunday to announce their QB1 for the Bengals game. Shortly after Jackson spoke, DraftKings Sportsbook had the Ravens as 1.5-point home favorites over the Bengals. It remains to be seen how that line will move, if at all, once outsiders learn whether Jackson or Huntley will be in the Baltimore lineup. Want more articles like this? home.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Eligible to Play vs. Ravens After NFL Reduces Discipline Upon Appeal
home.blurb: The Bills are on bye this week and will return to action on Nov. 1 in a marquee matchup with the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo has won back-to-back games after suffering its first loss of the season against the New England Patriots in Week 4. Bleacher Report • 7h Jaylen Brown Calls Out Tatum 🧢 Bleacher Report • 2h Bears TE Out for Season Buffalo Bills linebacker Sam Franklin Jr. will be eligible to play in Week 8 when the team returns from a bye after having his discipline reduced. Michael Signora, NFL senior vice president of football and international communications, announced on Friday that Franklin's appeal of his one-game suspension was reduced to a $14,926 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct by hearing officer James Thrash. The NFL announced on Wednesday that Franklin was being suspended for one game due to "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" during Buffalo's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. Franklin was said to have spit on a Raiders player during an extra-point attempt late in the fourth quarter. In a post on Instagram after the league announced its discipline, Franklin denied any wrongdoing: "Not a dirty player what so ever! Will always defend myself though. Still won't spit on anyone!" "As we said from the start, Sam did not and would never spit at an opponent, and there was no evidence that he did," Franklin's agents said in a statement . "We're glad the suspension was overturned and grateful to the hearing officer for a fair and thorough review. "It's unfortunate the league suspended Sam in the first place based on an unsupported accusation that received so much undeserved attention, and we hope the outcome is covered just as widely. We also hope the league takes a serious look at the opposing player's conduct, including striking Sam in the groin twice during the game. We're glad this is behind him, so Sam can get back to focusing on his teammates and next Sunday." Franklin was one of two Bills players disciplined for their actions during the Raiders game. C.J. Gardner-Johnson was suspended one game for spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. Officials flagged Gardner-Johnson for unsportsmanlike conduct and he was ejected from the game as a result of the incident. He issued an apology on social media following the Bills' win. Franklin is in his second season with the Bills after originally joining their practice squad in August 2025. He has appeared in 23 consecutive games since the start of last season. The 30-year-old Franklin has six combined tackles in six games in 2026. And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. Going to venerated Wembley Stadium, facing off against the division-leading Jaguars, who had the advantage of having played in England the week prior and didn't have to worry about their body clocks, and managing to get away with a win was huge for the Texans. Houston, now at 2-4 but having won two straight road games against division rivals, returns to NRG Stadium to host the New York Giants of New Jersey. The Giants, sitting at 3-2-1, come into this matchup atop the NFC East, despite not winning in their last two games, a tie at Washington and a loss against New Orleans. In their last game, they fell to the Saints 34-27, but the Saints held a lead of 34-10 at one point in the 4th Quarter. The Giants, forced to start backup QB Jameis Winston since starter Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury, decided to give recent trade acquisition J.J. McCarthy a chance in the 4th quarter. McCarthy went 11-of-21 for 243 yards for 1 TD and 1 INT, and had the Giants in position to possibly tie or win on the final Giants' drive of the game. The New York/New Jersey sports pages will have themselves a field day talking about the QB spot in this coming week. Likely because of that QB uncertainty, along with Houston's recent winning streak and the supposed talent disparity, the opening odds from FanDuel for the upcoming matchup between the Texans and the Giants are strongly supporting Houston at home: Overall, this may seem a bit high of an opening line. The Giants haven't played as difficult a schedule as Houston and they are coming in with key injuries and roster concerns. However, the Texans, even coming off a huge win against Jacksonville, are still struggling on defense and sit at 0-3 at home. They have only beaten the Giants once in 6 total meetings, and that was in 2002. Sandwiched between an international game and a bye week, this has the feel of a trap game for Houston. This particular line may tighten a bit as the week progresses, especially as the Giants sort out their QB situation and both teams sort out their respective injury situations. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. away.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
away.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. LS Zach Wood (calf) returned from injured reserve and is expected to play. The Saints don't have another long snapper on the roster. home.headline: Injury Report: Texans’ Growing Injury List Raises Stakes For Upcoming Game Against Giants
home.blurb: Tank Dell was a full participant in Houston's first official Week 7 practice as he prepares for his long-awaited return Sunday against the New York Giants. But seven Texans did not practice Wednesday because of injuries, including Azeez Al-Shaair, Reed Blankenship, Trent Brown, Blake Fisher, David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre and Dalton Schultz. Head coach DeMeco Ryans already confirmed earlier this week that Dell will play against New York. Wednesday's full participation is another encouraging step toward making that return a reality. Dell has been designated for return from injured reserve, and Houston has spent the past several weeks gradually increasing his practice work. Pitre did not practice because of his shoulder injury, while Blankenship was sidelined with concussion and hand issues. This is not the week to allow protection problems to return, since the Texans have a bye week following. Houston survived without Pitre in its 34-31 victory over Jacksonville, but losing multiple safeties would force the Texans to continue testing their depth. Calen Bullock already stepped up in London, recording his first interception of the season. Kamari Lassiter led the Texans with eight tackles while adding a pass defensed. Houston might need another big afternoon from that young secondary on Sunday. The interesting wrinkle is who will be throwing against it. New York coach John Harbaugh confirmed Wednesday that J.J. McCarthy will start against Houston. That should immediately put pressure on Houston's pass rush to make McCarthy uncomfortable. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals may be 2-4, but they're coming off a huge divisional victory over the Los Angeles Rams. The Cardinals are feeling it right now, and they're at home — but we know how Broncos Country travels, especially in the desert. At 4-2, the Broncos can't afford a slip-up — not if they want to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the division, and make their Week 8 rematch at Mile High a potential chance to get back to the top of the division, depending on what happens this Sunday with the Seattle Seahawks. That's me looking past the Cardinals a little bit. The Broncos won't be doing that. Sean Payton knows how to keep a team's focus on whichever game and opponent is up next, and that's the Cardinals. How will this one shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff see Sunday's action unfolding in Glendale, AZ. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 4-2 : Getting Bo Nix back in the flow of things has become like a quest for the Holy Grail. All the internal tinkering on Nix might not be as important as facing a Cardinals team the Broncos should beat. While most eyes will be focused on how Nix performs, it's returning rookie running back Jonah Coleman who steals the limelight with two scores. Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 4-2 : The Broncos' coaches and players are buzzing about a Nix breakout game. Looking at the Cardinals' 31st-ranked scoring defense — a unit allowing 350.5 yards per game — this is about as golden a get-right opportunity Nix could hope for. Courtland Sutton said , "At some point, the tide's going to turn" for Nix and this offense, and it happens at State Farm Stadium on Sunday. Nix passes for three touchdowns and 280 yards, while the Broncos romp in the desert. Pick : Broncos 27, Cardinals 17 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-2 : Only speaking for myself, the Broncos haven’t yet earned the benefit of the doubt. Not yet. But if there’s any way to earn that — and any day to have a get-right game — it’s Sunday against the Cardinals. This goes for the offense more so than the defense, which has been fantastic of late. If not now for Nix, then when? Go out there and dominate, and those “confidence issues” will miraculously disappear. I foresee a better showing, though maybe not quite the 2018 Kick Your A** blowout. This is an inferior opponent who, quite frankly, the Broncos should handily dispatch. “Should.” Pick : Broncos 30, Cardinals 16 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 4-2 : The Broncos' offense has been the source of much consternation. Is Nix hurt? Has the game passed Sean Payton by? Luckily, the Cardinals appear to be a get-right game. It's the NFL; there is no such thing as a guaranteed victory, but I expect the Broncos' defense and special teams, as well as continuity across the organization, to be felt in Arizona. I don't think the offense looks great... and even if it does, it's just one game, and the broader sample size should hold more weight in the total evaluation. Still, it will be nice to provide the fan base some hope. Pick : Broncos 20, Cardinals16 Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 4-2 : It's easy to think the Broncos will have their way with the Cardinals. But the Cardinals have shown they can challenge other teams , so it will be important for the Broncos' offense to come out strong. This won't be a dominant display, but it will be the first time this season both the Broncos' offense and defense play good complementary football, and Nix finds consistent success. Nix throws for a couple of touchdowns and rushes for another, giving fans some hope that he's close to being back. Pick : Broncos 24, Cardinals 13 Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 3-3 : If there was any opportunity to try to get the offense on track, it's this week against Arizona. Denver got the mini-bye, and Arizona's defense has allowed the most points in the league this season. Criticism of Nix is getting more intense by the minute, so it would be great to see him try to push the ball down the field and take chances against one of the worst defenses the league has to offer. I think he's gonna do it this week. Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 17 James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 2-4 : The Broncos are coming off a mini-bye, which frankly has come at a good time for a sputtering offense. Another week with Payton calling the plays again should be beneficial for Nix, but ultimately, the Broncos will have to play well to beat a tricky and plucky Cardinals team. The defense keys the win with a few takeaways off Jacoby Brissett, while the offense — just about — does enough to show some signs of life. The Broncos' defense should be able to carry it enough to allow the offense to work things out, and this is the best opportunity for Nix and company to do that, similarly to the Dallas Cowboys game a season ago. The Broncos show progress in Arizona, and while they don't fix everything in a week, they do walk out with the win. Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner's exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Denver : Thirty-first in total offense (252.2 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (84.2 YPG), 28th in passing offense (168.0 YPG), 26th in scoring offense (19.0 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total offense (307.3 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (96.3 YPG), 20th in passing offense (211.0 YPG), 24th in scoring offense (21.0 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-second in total defense (348.3 yards per game), 31st in rushing defense (139.8 YPG), 10th in passing defense (208.5 YPG), tied for 10th in scoring defense (20.8 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total defense (350.5 yards per game), 20th in rushing defense (120.8 YPG), 22nd in passing defense (229.7 YPG), tied for 31st in scoring defense (29.7 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the line of scrimmage on offense The Broncos offensive line has been the definition of "meh" to start the regular season. It's nowhere near what it's been the last few seasons, but it also isn't horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It's a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. Ya'll crazy if you think benching Bo Nix is even remotely the answer. That said, Bo Nix does need to play better, and he isn't seeing the field well to start the season. He's had slow starts in every season he's played, so, for now, I'm chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I'm hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos' schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. If the offense can up its game, this Broncos team will be unstoppable. — Sadaraine Limit the impact of Trey McBride The Broncos defense has performed well this season, aside from a few games. For the most part, they've been able to limit the impact of the opposing team's top player on their offense. This week, they face All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who is coming off a sensational 2025 season. He is the focal point of Arizona's aerial attack and gets over ten targets per game. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a good game plan that limits his impact on the game. If they can slow him down, Denver will have a great shot at earning their fifth victory of the season. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday's game?

away.headline: Broncos week 7 injury report: RB Tyler Badie trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday after missing the last four games. He still must be formally activated to the 53-man roster but is fully expected to play against the Cardinals. Coleman's return is especially helpful this week considering third-string RB Tyler Badie missed practice for a second straight day due to a thumb injury. His status for Sunday's game is in jeopardy; he needs a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up. Outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both also were DNPs this week. Hufanga will be ruled out on Friday, and the Broncos anticipate Elliss landing on short-term injured reserve, back at some point later this year. “He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," head coach Sean Payton said of Elliss on Wednesday. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) were limited participants; Surtain could be a game-time decision, though Waddle is expected to go. Arizona listed starting safety Budda Baker and running back Jeremiyah Love as DNP for a second consecutive day, as well as safety Andrew Wingard. Cornerback Garrett Williams and defensive lineman Darius Robinson were upgraded to limited. “They give you a couple different looks," Payton noted Wednesday. "They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback. I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.” Broncos Get Massive Boost with Return of RB Jonah Coleman Broncos' IR Watch: Who's Eligible to Return and What They Bring The Denver Broncos continued full-scale preparation for Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals, releasing their second injury report ahead of the Week 7 matchup. On it, running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) and cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) were listed as full practice participants for another day, while defensive end Zach Allen was upgraded to full after getting his usual rest day on Wednesday. Cardinals Might Be Down Some Starpower Unfortunately for the home team, the Cardinals are trending toward being at much less than full strength -- at least, according to their Thursday injury report . Baker's absence in particular would be a fortuitous break for a Broncos offense desperately seekin its first true breakout game in 2026. However, Payton knows well enough not to overlook the other 10 players on the Cardinals' defensive side. away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. away.headline: Jeremiyah Love, Walter Nolen III Get Final Injury Call For Cardinals-Broncos
away.blurb: Head coach Mike LaFleur has ruled out Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Walter Nolen III (ankle) among a few others for Week 7, which includes Andrew Wingard (knee) and Jon Gaines (knee). "All right, just to get this through. So Jeremiyah, Walt, and Dewey will all be out for Sunday, and then unfortunately, Jon Gaines had a practice injury yesterday, so he'll be out as well," LaFleur said. Arizona isn't expected to place Love or Nolen on injured reserve. Love will miss his second consecutive game while Nolen will be out for the first time in 2026. ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are going to be down some serious star power against the Denver Broncos. The Cardinals' coach also confirmed Carson Beck and Darius Robinson's injuries weren't serious. Budda Baker is also being monitored, but the team feels good about him according to LaFleur. This will massively hamper the Cardinals' chances to pull off another upset, this time coming against the Broncos — who are playing some of the toughest defense in the league. "I don't care what scheme you run on defense, as long as you have conviction in it, which they do. There's clarity with the players, which they do. You have good players that matches the scheme that they're trying to run, which they do. Like they're all on the same page," LaFleur said of Denver's defense. "Cover two, cover three, quarters, I mean, everyone has everything. It's how you're coaching it and how you're mixing and matching it, and what you know VJ [Vance Joseph] is thinking that he thinks is going to be best vs. us. We're going to get a little bit of everything. I'm assuming. I mean, that's usually what ends up happening. "And then there's specific areas where you're anticipating maybe a little bit more of this than that, based on who we have compared to maybe based on some other teams. You never really know exactly what you're going to see. You just go off of what you saw on tape, some of your past experiences. But as we know, this defense has been playing really well for a few years, and it's going to be a challenge not only because of the scheme, but because of the players that are actually running the scheme." The Cardinals will release their final practice reports for today, though Arizona clearly will be down some massive names. away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses.
