Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. picks.headline: Lions vs. Packers preview, prediction: On Paper
picks.blurb: Lions vs. Packers preview, prediction: On Paper - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Lions vs. Packers preview, prediction: On Paper DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions plays against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jeremy Reisman Fri, October 23, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 12 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers are in town for a big NFC North matchup. The division is establishing themselves as one of the best in the NFL, so whoever wins this game will make an important statement, while the loser will have a bit of a hole to climb out of with three losses on the year. Which team has the statistical edge? Let's take a look in our On Paper Lions vs. Packers preview and prediction. Lions pass offense (13th in DVOA) vs. Packers pass defense (2nd) The Lions' passing attack continues to be one of the more reliable units on the team. Jared Goff has been amazingly consistent throughout his Lions career, producing a top-10 or top-five unit for four years running. Thus far this season, Detroit ranks: Second in passer rating (111.3) Seventh in yards per attempt (7.8) Third in dropback EPA (0.304) Fifth in dropback success rate (50.9%) Aiding Goff's MVP-like campaign is an offensive line that has come together quicker than expected. The Lions rank fourth in ESPN's pass block win rate (58%), third in PFF pass blocking grade (73.2), 11th in pressure rate allowed (32.4%), and 13th in sack percentage (5.4%). There has been some issues when it comes to blitzes (time to pressure is third-highest at 2.21), but that hasn't stopped Goff from being extremely efficient against the blitz (+0.33 EPA/pass, second-best). The only big question with this unit is how the return of starting center Cade Mays will impact the unit. Will he be an immediate upgrade from Juice Scruggs, who played well? Or will there be an acclimation period that will result in some missed assignments? The Packers are the most formidable foe the Lions have faced this year when it comes to defending the pass. Now, it's important to note that they have faced a few backup quarterbacks this year, including Carson Wentz, Jalon Daniels, Case Keenum, and Tyson Bagent. Still, last week's performance against the Cowboys was impressive, and shouldn't be pushed to the side. Thus far, Green Bay ranks: Third in passer rating allowed (73.9) Third in yards per attempt (5.9) Seventh in dropback EPA (-0.024) 14th in dropback success rate (45.5%) That last stat suggests a unit that may be bolstered a bit by big plays. And, indeed, that is at least part of the case. The Packers have successfully created a lot of sacks (15, 12th) and turnovers (nine interceptions, first). That is due to the aggressive nature of this defense. They make up for a mediocre defensive line with a high blitz rate (31.7%, 13th) and disguised coverages thanks to their elite pair of safeties. They rank second in total pressures (100), fourth in pressure rate (41.2%), and ninth in average time to pressure (2.58). They are able to do that despite ranking 30th in pass rush win rate (42%) and 26th in PFF's pass-rush grade (63.8). So if the Lions can manage the Packers' aggressive tendencies and avoid negative plays, this is a winnable matchup. Player to watch: Cade Mays. In his first game as a Lion, he may be one of the more critical pieces for the team. His presnap reads are going to be essential to Detroit's success, but that is something the Lions believe is one of his strengths. Via OC Drew Petzing: There's a stability factor there. He plays at a high level. He's big, he's physical, he's really smart. The communication piece is a huge part of playing that position. Advantage: Lions +1. This is a pretty dang even matchup, but the reason I'm giving the Lions an edge is because I believe Green Bay feeds off disruption, and Detroit has done a pretty good job avoiding that. Goff has yet to turn the ball over, and while I expect the Packers to get to the Lions quarterback for a few sacks, that shouldn't be enough to take them completely out of their rhythm. If the Packers are forced to blitz, Goff has proven he can beat that. Lions run offense (2nd) vs. Packers run defense (27th) It's been very feast or famine for the Lions' rushing attack, yet most of the statistics actually show this as a near-elite unit despite the inconsistencies. The Lions rank: 12th in yards per carry (4.4) Eighth in rush EPA (-0.033) Fifth in success rate (46.2%) Detroit is still seeking its first true explosive run, with Jahmyr Gibbs' longest rush of the season being just 22 yards, but it seems like it's just a matter of time given the underlying success of the unit. Run blocking is among the league's best, ranking first in PFF grade (78.1), fourth in adjusted line yards, and 20th in run-block win rate (72%). However, short-yardage situations have been a problem: the Lions rank just 20th in power success rate (62%) and they've been stuffed on 18% of rushes, which ranks 21st. Still, Gibbs has been impressive. His 18 rushes of 10+ yards ranks third in the NFL, despite playing one fewer game than most backs. Okay, so this is where things are going to look a little weird. On the surface, the Packers have been pretty darn good against the run. They've held half of their opponents below 90 rushing yards and four of six below 3.5 yards per carry. But they also got completely smashed by the Falcons, and some of their down-to-down consistency is not as good as the raw numbers look. Overall, the Packers rank: 15th in yards per carry allowed (4.0) 27th in rush EPA (-0.042) 25th in success rate (42.5%) How much is that being dragged down by the Falcons game? Not as much as you think. In the three games since playing Atlanta, Green Bay still ranks just 28th in rush EPA and 27th in success rate. If we include the Falcons game, over the last four weeks, the Packers rank 32nd in rush EPA and t-32nd in success rate. In other words, this is much more of a mismatch than it looks like. Player to watch: Javon Bullard. The Packers' nickel corner/safety is a force in the run game and will have to be accounted for on every play. Not only does he have a 85.3 PFF run defense grade, but he also has three tackles for loss. Advantage: Lions +2. I'm curious to see how involved the Packers' secondary will be in the run game because if they devote too many bodies to defend Gibbs, it could make them vulnerable on the back end. Still, I think this is a pretty clear advantage in Detroit's favor, but I'm capping the advantage at just two because the Lions have been inconsistent, and the Packers' "poor" run defense has really only cost them in one game. Packers pass offense (17th) vs. Lions pass defense (25th) It seems like the Packers' passing attack is in the midst of turning a corner—and that corner is finding an offensive line combination that isn't a complete disaster. Through the first couple of games, the Packers could barely field an offense due to injuries and subpar play along the offensive line. It's gotten a little better with some shuffling and additions, but the overall season numbers are still very concerning for Green Bay. They rank 25th in pressure rate, 32nd in time to pressure, 27th in pressures allowed, 32nd in pass-block win rate, and 32nd in PFF's pass-blocking grade. Yet, because they have very good weapons and a solid quarterback, their overall stats aren't as bad as you may think. The Packers rank: 15th in passer rating (91.8) 12th in yards per attempt (7.5) 14th in dropback EPA (0.131) 21st in dropback success rate (42.9%) Now, if you look at just the last three weeks, the Packers offense is clearly improving: Ninth in passer rating (101.8) Seventh in yards per attempt (8.2) Sixth in dropback EPA (0.248) 14th in dropback success rate (47.1%) As we've talked about all week, it's the Packers' deep ball that is most concerning this week, as Jordan Love airs it out more than any other quarterback in the league. The Lions' passing defense has been downright horrible, and you don't need me to show you the stats to prove it… but I'm going to anyways. Detroit ranks: 29th in passer rating allowed (106.3) 22nd in yards per attempt (7.5) 28th in dropback EPA (0.261) 30th in dropback success rate (52.7%) While big plays have been a huge problem (23 pass plays of 20+ yards allowed, third most), the high success rate allowed suggests there is no inflation with any of the other stats: they're just bad across the board. Even last game's "success" against the Cardinals looks more like playing a bad offense than playing good defense. But there is one saving grace, and it's the Lions' pass rush. Detroit sports PFF's third-highest pass-rush grade, ESPN's third-highest pass-rush win rate, and the fourth-highest sack rate in the NFL. Unfortunately, that only highlights how bad the coverage aspect of this team has been. Could the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch help? Absolutely. But I'm not ready to credit him as a huge difference-maker in his first game back from an Achilles. Player to watch: Matthew Golden. Of the Packers' 32 deep-ball attempts, 15 of them have targeted Golden. The second-year receiver has caught four of those for 173 yards (third-most deep ball yardage in NFL). That may not seem like a ton, but those are obviously four huge-impact plays, each gaining at least 36 yards. Advantage: Packers +3. Yeah, this is a pretty big advantage to give the Packers, but they're trending in the right direction, and the Lions are one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Yes, you could technically say the Lions are trending in the right direction after their performance against the Cardinals, but I am not convinced considering how poor Arizona's pass offense is. I expect a very strong day from Love. Packers run offense (32nd) vs. Lions run defense (23rd) I don't think there is any doubt in the world that the Packers' have the worst rushing attack in football. Their numbers are downright atrocious for the season. They've yet to hit 90 rushing yards in a game, nor have they rushed for over 3.5 a carry in a contest. For the year, they rank: 32nd in yards per carry (2.9) 32nd in rush EPA (-0.299) 31st in rush success rate (32.%) Unsurprisingly, the issues are mainly on the patchworked offensive line. They rank 31st in PFF's run-blocking grade (47.8), 32nd in adjusted line yards, but oddly 15th in ESPN's run block win rate. They rank 29th in rushing yards before contract per rush (0.74), and also 30th in rushing yards after contact per rush (2.26). That second number certainly has a chance to improve with Josh Jacobs expected back this week because Green Bay's running backs have also been poor (the Packers rank 32nd in rushing yards over expected per rush). But there is clearly a systemic issue here that Jacobs can't fix on his own. Last year, Jacobs actually ranked 33rd out of 35 running backs in EPA/rush, so he is not the savior Packers fans are hoping for. It's hard to get a grasp on the Lions' run defense. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions for Green Bay Packers vs Detroit Lions Matchup at Ford Field - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview 4 Bold Predictions for Green Bay Packers vs Detroit Lions Matchup at Ford Field Let’s dive into our bold predictions for Sunday’s Packers vs Lions matchup. The last time the Packers lost, Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson received 31 touches and turned them into 213 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. Detroit should aim to give Jahmyr Gibbs a relatively similar workload on Sunday afternoon. The Lions’ offense already boasts the fifth-highest Rush Success rate (46.2 percent) in the NFL this season, and it’s facing a defense that ranks 25th in Success Rate (45.5 percent) allowed on the ground. Green Bay is also even worse without linebacker Edgerrin Cooper and defensive tackle Javon Hargrave, making this a ripe matchup for Detroit to exploit. In a game where we expect Gibbs to receive 28-plus touches, he’ll turn those opportunities into 180-plus scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. The breakout year Green Bay hoped to get from Matthew Golden is happening. In his second NFL season, Golden currently ranks seventh in yards per reception (16.7) and sixth in receiving yards (501). Even with some drops mixed in, he’s put up 100-plus receiving yards in three of his last four games, and the lone outlier (Oct. 4) came with a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Assuming D.J. Reed sees more time in coverage against Christian Watson, Golden should be able to thrive in his matchup against Ennis Rakestraw Jr. We certainly wouldn’t rule out 100-plus yards and a score, but we’ll make the slightly more conservative projection by saying Golden finds the end zone or hits the 100-yard mark. Jared Goff has been sensational this season from the pocket. Entering Week 7, he boasts a 111.3 passer rating with 12 passing touchdowns and a 67 percent completion rate, averaging nearly 300 passing yards per game. With Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams drawing coverage from Brandon Cisse and Keisean Nixon, there’ll be ample opportunities for Goff to maintain his perfect TD-INT ratio and push closer to 2,000 passing yards on the season. On the other side, now that he has adequate pass protection, Jordan Love is playing MVP-caliber football and about to take on a defense that has allowed the fourth-highest completion rate (68.1 percent) and the most passing yards per game ( 297.4 ) to opponents. We’re expecting a shootout, with Love (275-plus passing yards and 3 touchdowns) and Goff (260-plus yards and two touchdowns) challenging for 600-plus total yards. Home-field advantage does matter here, but it’s not a major difference-maker since both offenses should thrive playing indoors. What we view as the biggest X-factor in this Packers vs. Lions matchup is the defense we trust more. Even without Micah Parsons, Green Bay has allowed the third-lowest scoring rate (29.9 percent) and the 10th-fewest points per drive (1.85), whereas Detroit has allowed the eighth-highest scoring rate (44.4 percent) and the most points per drive (2.81). The Lions’ ability to run the football and the return of Brian Branch means there is a very good chance they come out on top at home. However, with Josh Jacobs rejoining the Packers’ offense in Week 7, we’ll give Green Bay the slight edge because of a higher level of confidence in its defense generating a few more stops. 1 / 10 4 Bold Predictions for Green Bay Packers vs Detroit Lions Matchup at Ford Field Sunday afternoon’s Week 7 NFC North rivalry matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions won’t deliver nearly the hatred we get to see between Green Bay and Chicago. away.headline: Packers’ final injury report before Cowboys game puts 2 defensive position groups under the microscope
away.blurb: DT Jonathan Ford (out – calf) DT Javon Hargrave (out – Achilles) WR Skyy Moore (out – ankle) CB Benjamin St-Juste (out – hamstring) DT Jordon Riley (doubtful – Achilles) G Aaron Banks (questionable – knee/toe) DT Anthony Campbell (questionable – ankle) CB Brandon Cisse (questionable – hip) G Jacob Monk (questionable – quadricep) WR Savion Williams (questionable – ankle) Cornerback Keisean Nixon opened the week as a non-participant on Wednesday with a groin injury, but head coach Matt LaFleur had already confirmed in his press conference that Nixon will play. The veteran returned to practice on a limited basis Thursday, opening the gates for his availability against Dallas. On the other hand, rookie second-rounder Brandon Cisse was added to the injury report with a hip injury. He was limited on Friday and is questionable to play. Meanwhile, backup cornerback Benjamin St-Juste has a hamstring injury and did not practice at all. He's already been ruled out. The other position with plenty of reasons for concern is defensive tackle. Green Bay started the regular season with seven defensive tackles on the 53-man roster, but injuries have taken a toll on the group . Warren Brinson is on injured reserve with a groin injury. Javon Hargrave remains on the 53-man roster, but he is out for the season with a ruptured Achilles and is ruled out against the Cowboys. He will eventually move to injured reserve as well. Three more defensive tackles appeared on the report through the week, but Devonte Wyatt (ankle) is off the report and good to go. Jonathan Ford, who has a calf injury, did not practice at all and will not play. Anthony Campbell is also dealing with an ankle injurie, and he's questionable. Therefore, the only defensive tackles who are fully healthy going into Sunday are Karl Brooks and rookie third-rounder Chris McClellan. For a position that started the season as one of the deepest on the roster, that's a significant shift in a short period of time. The good news is that defensive tackle Jordon Riley is working his way back from an Achilles injury. He got hurt late last season and started this season on the physically unable to perform list, but the Packers have now designated him to return. That doesn't necessarily mean Riley will play against Dallas. The Packers first have to activate him to the 53-man roster before he can suit up. He was limited at practice throughout the week, though. There's at least a chance he returns, if not this week, then next week against the Detroit Lions. Given the state of the interior defensive line, getting Riley back would give Green Bay a much-needed body in the rotation. Kick returner and wide receiver Skyy Moore injured his ankle against the Chicago Bears, and he's out. Savion Williams (still on IR), Jacob Monk, and Aaron Banks are all questionable. away.headline: Packers LB Zaire Franklin’s status for Lions bout revealed in latest injury update
away.blurb: Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions after he suffered a shin injury during practice on Thursday. Head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Friday that the veteran defensive captain has been ruled out . With Franklin unavailable, Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper are expected to take on larger responsibilities. McDuffie has started in Cooper’s place over the past two weeks, while Hopper, a 2024 third-round draft pick, could receive an opportunity to play a more regular defensive role. Nick Niemann and veteran special-teamer Kristian Welch are also options for the linebacker rotation. Related: Packers’ Josh Jacobs is trending toward playing vs. Lions amid controversial return Franklin’s absence creates another challenge for Green Bay’s defense, which has already lost starting linebacker Edgerrin Cooper for the season because of an Achilles tendon tear. Cooper suffered the injury in Week 4, leaving the Packers without both of their Week 1 starting linebackers for the trip to Detroit. LaFleur indicated that Franklin is not expected to require injured reserve, which would force him to miss at least four games. However, the team is still assessing the severity of his injury. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 30-year-old has been a key contributor through six games, leading the Packers with 48 tackles and ranking second on the team with 15 stops, according to Pro Football Focus. He has also played 414 defensive snaps this season. Green Bay will face a big test against the Lions’ running game, led by running back Jahmyr Gibbs. He has recorded 504 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns, ranking fifth in the NFL in rushing yards and tied for second in rushing scores. He has also produced 27 receptions for 243 yards and two receiving touchdowns. Detroit’s offense is averaging 32.8 points per game, tied with the Buffalo Bills for the league lead. The Lions have also exploited McDuffie in the past as quarterback Jared Goff completed all nine passes thrown toward the linebacker in their 2024 meeting, producing 68 yards and a touchdown in the team’s 34-31 win . The timing of his latest injury could hardly be worse for Franklin, as the Packers are scheduled to play on Thursday Night Football in Week 8, potentially extending his absence to a second game. It would be a rare setback for the defender, who had missed only one game throughout his NFL career before the latest setback. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. away.headline: Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin won't play Sunday at Detroit because of a shin injury
away.blurb: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Friday that Franklin took a knee to the shin during a collision and wouldn’t be available for the Lions game. Franklin had been added to the injury report on Thursday. GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay linebacker Zaire Franklin has a shin injury that will keep him from playing Sunday at Detroit, leaving the Packers without their second-leading tackler. “I don’t think it’s going to be anything too long-term, but just an unfortunate deal,” LaFleur said. “It happens when you play football, especially the way our guys have been practicing. But I think we’ve got a lot of confidence in (Isaiah) McDuffie and (Ty’Ron) Hopper and Nick Niemann if need be to go in there and do a great job for us.” Franklin has 41 tackles in his first year with Green Bay after spending eight seasons with the Indianapolis Colts. The Packers acquired him in a trade for defensive tackle Colby Wooden. Green Bay’s top tackler is safety Evan Williams, who has 49 stops. The Packers (4-2) will be seeking their fourth straight win Sunday when they face the Lions (3-2). See AP’s full NFL coverage here

Bryant initially signed with the New England Patriots as an undrafted free agent in 2020, appearing in 55 games and starting 17 with the Pats from 2020-23. home.headline: Detroit Lions address return game, sign DeAndre Carter to active roster
home.blurb: “I think DeAndre Carter’s got a lot of experience. He’ll probably step in and return punts for us and kickoffs for us in the game, along with (Jacob) Saylors. And we’ll just keep going as it’s been,” Lions special teams coordinator Dave Fipp said Thursday. After Tom Kennedy suffered a season-ending injury at the Arizona Cardinals , the Lions needed to act fast to find a replacement return man. Although practice squad receivers Lucky Jackson and Dominic Lovett were in the mix for the crucial special teams role, Carter’s experience was viewed as the deciding factor. Carter played four games with Cleveland last season and has extensive return-game experience over an eight-season NFL career with the Eagles , Texans , Bears , Commanders , Chargers , Raiders , and Browns. The 5-foot-8, 190-pound receiver and return man has caught 117 passes for 1,331 yards and six touchdowns across 111 games played. Carter has returned 155 punts for 1,508 yards and 9.7 yards per punt return. The Sacramento State product has returned 144 kickoffs for 3,399 yards and one touchdown, averaging 23.6 yards per kick return. This article originally appeared on Lions Wire: Detroit Lions address return game, sign DeAndre Carter to active roster On Thursday, the Detroit Lions (3-2) announced that recently-signed practice squad wide receiver and specialist DeAndre Carter had been signed to the active roster. Carter will serve as the team's designated punt returner and help with kick returns. "I just come in and do what I do, man. This is a business, and I come in and I work, try to take care of my part, and then if it's what the coaches want, it's what the coaches want," Carter told Brad Galli Thursday . "I'm just grateful for the opportunity that they gave me here to play and contribute to this team and to the unit. I'm excited about it." The Lions and Packers are scheduled to kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday, Oct. 25 at Ford Field, with play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt and color analyst Tom Brady calling the game, and Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi reporting from the sidelines for FOX. picks.headline: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are preparing to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, and the injuries just keep piling up. Earlier this week , the Rams placed wide receiver Davante Adams and nose tackle Poona Ford on injured reserve. Additionally, defensive lineman Kobie Turner has been ruled out for a handful of weeks. “Trent will be a DNP with his groin. We'll take it a day at a time, like what I told you guys, and evaluate his status as we go,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Then on Monday, found out Landman landed in the concussion protocol so he'll be a DNP.” While Landman's presence on the injury report isn’t surprising given that he’s been there the last few weeks, his placement in the concussion protocol is certainly a new development. In order to return to play, Landman will be limited in his allowed activity. He’ll then graduate to an aerobic exercise program overseen by the club’s medical staff. Lastly, after leaving Kobie Turner off the injured reserve transactions on Tuesday alongside Davante Adams and Poona Ford, the Rams placed him on injured reserve Wednesday. Turner will be out for a minimum of four weeks. In corresponding moves, the Rams signed EDGE Darryl Peterson III to the active roster and signed Jalen Hunt to the practice squad. “Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever and they're like, 'I have to trade a guy in and out now.' We're like, 'Well, that guy has worked his ass off for the last eight months to get this opportunity and it's unfortunate he doesn't get to do what he loves to do,’” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “I feel more for our guys than I do for anybody else.I know the work that they put into it to be out here doing what they love, so that hurts me for them. But at the same time, I think I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win.” For the Raiders, defensive lineman Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant as he remains in the concussion protocol. away.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua questionable vs. Raiders due to calf injury
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams don't yet know whether Puka Nacua will suit up for them on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders . Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua will not practice on Friday and will officially be listed as questionable to play in Vegas. Nacua has already missed two games this season, sitting out Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip/groin injury. The Rams are already without Davante Adams, who ruptured his hamstring in Week 6 and will now miss 6-10 weeks. Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell could all see increased snaps with Adams out, and will become even bigger parts of the offense if Nacua misses Sunday's game. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams WR Puka Nacua questionable vs. Raiders due to calf injury Nacua left Thursday's practice early after injuring his calf. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Friday that the injury is considered "more minor than anything else," and his status for Week 7 is "up in the air." This season, Nacua has 37 catches for 417 yards and a touchdown in the four games he's played. He also has three carries for 11 yards and a rushing touchdown. The Rams and Raiders kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET, which means inactives will be due 90 minutes ahead of time at 2:55 p.m. ET. At that point, we will officially know what his status is for the game.

away.headline: Rams OLB Myles Garrett likely to return to practice next week
away.blurb: With all the bad news, the Rams were in need of some positivity and got it on Friday morning. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports that Garrett is likely to return to practice next week , which will be his first time practicing since Week 1. The Rams traded Jared Verse and draft picks for Garrett this offseason in hopes he would be the pass rusher that gets the franchise back to the Super Bowl. When Garrett returns, he will have to help the Rams dig themselves out of a 2-4 hole that has them sitting in last in the division. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams OLB Myles Garrett likely to return to practice next week The Los Angeles Rams ' hopes of a dominant season were crushed last week, and to make things worse, the team lost several players to injured reserve . Davante Adams, Kobie Turner and Poona Ford all joined Myles Garrett on IR after getting hurt in Sunday's loss. "I was told for Myles Garrett that it is likely he returns to practice next week, which would be about seven or eight weeks from the injury. So, could potentially play Week 8," said Rapoport. That means not only is Garrett likely to practice next week, but he could also play. The Rams face the Los Angeles Chargers in that contest. Garrett has only played in one game this year, the season-opener, before lingering knee issues that were exacerbated in the offseason forced the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year to address the injury with surgery and a stint on injured reserve.

away.headline: Rams rule out top linebacker vs. Raiders this Sunday
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: An already injury-riddled Los Angeles Rams defense will be without another top defender this week as team captain and defensive signal caller Nate Landman has been ruled out. On top of Landman's absence, the unit lost Poona Ford for the season and Kobie Turner to short-term injured reserve this week, while Myles Garrett is still waiting to return. Landman is the team's leading tackler, recording 27 solo and 51 total tackles. With Landman out, the team has Omar Speights, Shaun Dolac, and Grant Stuard on their roster, and they will elevate Eric Kendricks off the practice squad. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams rule out top linebacker vs. Raiders this Sunday Landman will not play after entering the concussion protocol this week. The linebacker has never missed a game in his Rams career and is a pivotal part of their defensive structure, featuring in 71 of the 72 defensive snaps played last week against the Arizona Cardinals . He also has two forced fumbles thanks to his excellent execution of the "peanut punch" on ball carriers. It's not known at this time who will be the defensive signal-caller will be on defense, but Quentin Lake has performed the job before, and he plays every snap; thus, he's presumed to take the role. The Rams take on the Las Vegas Raiders this week at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday.

home.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua questionable vs. Raiders due to calf injury
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams don't yet know whether Puka Nacua will suit up for them on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders . Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua will not practice on Friday and will officially be listed as questionable to play in Vegas. Nacua has already missed two games this season, sitting out Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip/groin injury. The Rams are already without Davante Adams, who ruptured his hamstring in Week 6 and will now miss 6-10 weeks. Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell could all see increased snaps with Adams out, and will become even bigger parts of the offense if Nacua misses Sunday's game. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams WR Puka Nacua questionable vs. Raiders due to calf injury Nacua left Thursday's practice early after injuring his calf. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Friday that the injury is considered "more minor than anything else," and his status for Week 7 is "up in the air." This season, Nacua has 37 catches for 417 yards and a touchdown in the four games he's played. He also has three carries for 11 yards and a rushing touchdown. The Rams and Raiders kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET, which means inactives will be due 90 minutes ahead of time at 2:55 p.m. ET. At that point, we will officially know what his status is for the game.

home.headline: Rams rule out top linebacker vs. Raiders this Sunday
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: An already injury-riddled Los Angeles Rams defense will be without another top defender this week as team captain and defensive signal caller Nate Landman has been ruled out. On top of Landman's absence, the unit lost Poona Ford for the season and Kobie Turner to short-term injured reserve this week, while Myles Garrett is still waiting to return. Landman is the team's leading tackler, recording 27 solo and 51 total tackles. With Landman out, the team has Omar Speights, Shaun Dolac, and Grant Stuard on their roster, and they will elevate Eric Kendricks off the practice squad. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams rule out top linebacker vs. Raiders this Sunday Landman will not play after entering the concussion protocol this week. The linebacker has never missed a game in his Rams career and is a pivotal part of their defensive structure, featuring in 71 of the 72 defensive snaps played last week against the Arizona Cardinals . He also has two forced fumbles thanks to his excellent execution of the "peanut punch" on ball carriers. It's not known at this time who will be the defensive signal-caller will be on defense, but Quentin Lake has performed the job before, and he plays every snap; thus, he's presumed to take the role. The Rams take on the Las Vegas Raiders this week at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday.

home.headline: Mike Washington Jr.'s injury is throwing wrench into Raiders' perfect RB plan
home.blurb: For weeks, many have advocated for Washington Jr. to get a larger snap share, not just because Jeanty is banged up, but because he has something to offer, and it would keep defenses on their toes. In Week 6 against the Bills, though, the Raiders pretty much had it figured out. It's not like the Raiders suddenly had the ground game figured out; they ran for only 65 yards. But Jeanty did get his first rushing touchdown of the year, and Las Vegas had its highest yards per carry since Week 3, and its second-highest since Week 1. It was better , even though it wasn't good . Being a limited participant on Wednesday isn't always a red flag, as teams typically take the first practice of the week to let players get healthy or give them time off. But Washington Jr. was downgraded to a non-participant on Thursday, which is worrisome. His status for Sunday is in doubt. The Las Vegas Raiders need to fix their rushing attack if they want to reach their goals this year. Klint Kubiak seems hellbent on establishing the run, and rightfully so, but whatever they've been doing to begin the 2026 NFL season has not worked at all. They are currently 30th in the NFL in total rushing yards and 31st in yards per attempt. Neither the totals nor the efficiency has been good. And while history suggests that patience is required for Kubiak's run game to take flight, things were never this bad with the Seattle Seahawks. The Raiders have an issue, both with their run-blocking and with their running backs not seeing or taking advantage of the lanes that are actually paved. But last week against the Buffalo Bills, the run game was better, at least incrementally. And that's because Las Vegas deployed a different strategy with different splits and usage for Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. The latter being injured, however, could throw a wrench into things. Raiders deployed ideal RB splits and usage in Week 6 vs. Bills It has been apparent all season that Jeanty is not playing at full strength. Kubiak won't admit that, but Jeanty has said himself multiple times that he "hopes to be 100% soon," or something of that ilk. That is a big reason why he doesn't look as explosive and the run game is suffering with his high usage. Instead of running Jeanty into the ground, they only played him on 57.6 percent of the snaps, and they put in Washington Jr. for 34.8 percent. But sparing Jeanty some reps was not the only thing that made sense about this setup. Jeanty only ran the ball 10 times in his 38 snaps, but he was heavily involved in the passing game. Rather than having him pound the ball between the tackles and get beat up more, he was targeted six times and caught four passes for 36 yards. So, Jeanty still got a good amount of touches, but there was less wear and tear on his body. Washington Jr. played a career high in snaps as a result, and tied his career high in both carries and touches. He ran 9 times for 43 yards, which is 4.8 yards per carry, and he caught a 7-yard pass. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. This weekend, Seattle will host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City is coming off a frustrating 2025 campaign, which ended with a record of 6-11. That was the first time they had a losing season under Andy Reid, and they've already turned things around. Much of that is due to Kenneth Walker III, the former Seahawk who has been electric for the Chiefs . Seattle needs to find a way to contain Walker, while also figuring out how to get their ground game on track, which could happen with Zach Charbonnet set to return to action. To make matters worse, Deebo Samuel Sr. is also currently sidelined, which could leave Purdy with veteran Brandin Cooks as his top wideout. San Francisco is going to need firepower to keep pace with the pesky Falcons, who are led by Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Mike Kadlick Week 7 Upset Pick Miami Dolphins (+190) vs. New York Jets It’s time for the Dolphins to notch their first win of the Jeff Hafley era. While Miami currently owns the NFL’s worst offense and a bottom-10 defense, they’re coming off a bye week and are playing a Jets team that has lost four of its last five games. Though they’ve played competitively for the most part, New York has still yet to find an identity under coach Aaron Glenn and could be ripe for the taking after losing to the Patriots in Foxborough in Week 6. I think Miami finds their way to victory on Sunday at MetLife. Iain MacMillan Week 7 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+140) vs. Carolina Panthers It's time to sell high on this Panthers team. Their offense has been phenomenal to start the year, but I have plenty of questions surrounding the ability of some of the defenses they've had to face. Once they started facing top-10 defenses, I wouldn't be surprised to see them significantly regress. It could start this weekend when they take on a Tampa Bay defense that's fourth in opponent EPA per play and eighth in opponent success rate. I'm going to get in on the Bucs early this week and hope that Baker Mayfield ends up returning to action. If he starts on Sunday, we'll likely get some nice closing line value on the Buccaneers. Yet, I’m taking Kansas City to win outright on the road and improve to 6-0. The Chiefs have found a new dynamic with Kenneth Walker III and this running game, and I expect the reigning Super Bowl MVP to have a major workload against his former team. Mahomes is a shocking 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up as a road underdog in his career, and he’s by far the better quarterback in this game. Sam Darnold has doomed Seattle at times this season, throwing seven picks in four games since returning from a glute injury. The Seahawks offense has been extremely reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and it ranks 25th in the league in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate. If you're looking for player props and game-day value, check out the latest lines at FanDuel Sportsbook before kickoff. The Seattle Seahawks are coming off of two straight losses and are staring a sub .500 record straight in the eyes. The Chiefs meanwhile are undefeated and are currently elated with their recent running back signing (and Offensive Player of the Year candidate) Kenneth Walker III. Let's look at some game picks ahead of this matchup Sunday Night. Kenneth Walker III over 84.5 rushing yards (-114) I know Walker III is not a Seahawk anymore. However, considering his dominance this season, and the Seahawks lack of dominant running game, this is surely the game pick on the top of everyone's mind. Walker III is averaging 133 yards per game this season . Meanwhile the Seahawks defense has not allowed a 100 yard rusher in a franchise record, 35 games – not since October 27, 2024. One of these juggernauts will have to break in this matchup. The betting line being at 84.5 seems to be lower than many expected, or at least lower than I expected. Walker III is on a career heater right now. His ability to flip the field at any moment and break any run into a house call is very rare. Even if the Seahawks defense holds Walker III in check, it only takes one explosive run to get close to this 84.5 line. On top of this, Walker III already gets a large share of carries, and is now facing a revenge game. I would expect Walker III to get a ton of carries in this game, which means tons of opportunities to hit this line. All of this considered, it is tough to see Walker III not being able to hit at least 85 yards rushing. That doesn't mean that he will break 100 yards – the Seahawks could still very easily extend their streak to 36 games. However, this will be their hardest challenge yet. The pick: Kenneth Walker III over 84.5 rushing yards . Over 42.5 points (-112) The line for this game is 42.5, also a little lower. The Seahawks have scored at least 29 points four times this season. Their only two games where they scored less was in Week 1 with Drew Lock coming in with no first team reps, and in Week 6 with a short week Thursday Night Football game. Add to this, the fact that the Seahawks are playing the red hot Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs. There is a good chance that the Seahawks offense will need to keep up with Kansas City and their elite running game. That will surely be easier to do with Anthony Bradford and Zach Charbonnet likely returning for this game. Expect a high scoring affair in the battle of former AFC West foes. The pick: Over 42.5 total points (-112) . Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 92.5 receiving yards (-114). Leading the NFL in receptions (49), receiving yards (717), and receiving touchdowns (7) , JSN is once again on a heater. JSN has only missed the receiving yards line once this season – week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers where he put up only 76 yards (18.5 yards shy of the line). With the Seahawks run game struggling, and Sam Darnold looking less confident week in and week out, expect the safety blanket, JSN to have another big game this week against the Chiefs. Despite averaging 143.4 yards per game, the lines still remain fairly low. With it this low, the smartest move would be to bet the over. The pick: Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 92.5 receiving yards . Zach Charbonnet to score 2+ touchdowns (+750) The first three picks may not be too risky. However, this last pick is very risky. Trying to correctly guess who will score two or more touchdowns is a Hail Mary of sorts, but why not live on the edge? Charbonnet, who was just activated off of the PUP list , is expected to make his season debut against the Chiefs. This season, the Seahawks have struggled in short yardage situations. That is exactly where Charbonnet's return is huge. When on the field, Charbonnet tends to find the end zone. Last season, Charbonnet led the Seahawks with 12 touchdowns. The year prior, Charbonnet had 8 touchdowns . Although this will be his first game back since tearing his ACL in the 2025 playoffs, look to see Charbonnet get these opportunities once again. It isn't just the short yardage situations however. Charbonnet is also a strong pass catcher and gives the Seahawks an opportunity to score as a receiver as well. Despite only having one career receiving touchdown, Charbonnet still has 95 receptions for 693 yards in his young three year career. The other elephant in the room with Charbonnet's return is Kenneth Walker III's absence. Throughout his career Charbonnet has always split the backfield with Walker III. However, this season Charbonnet has an opportunity to prove he is the clear number one running back. With Jadarian Price still on injured reserve, and the other running backs on the roster proving lackluster, this week will be a perfect opportunity for Charbonnet to prove he can lead this backfield. The pick: Zach Charbonnet to score 2+ touchdowns .

The Seattle Seahawks' willingness to let Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III walk in free agency was tied to doubts regarding his injury history, ESPN's Nate Taylor and Brady Henderson reported Friday. According to Taylor and Henderson, Seahawks "decision-makers had reservations about [Walker's] availability dating to his rookie season." Because of those reservations, the Seahawks were "only willing to go as high as roughly $10 million per season to re-sign him in March," Taylor and Henderson reported. Taylor and Henderson reported concerns regarding Walker's early-career injuries also contributed to the Seahawks drafting Zach Charbonnet in 2023 and a backfield split between Charbonnet and Walker last season. After he was selected by the Seahawks in the second round of the 2022 draft, Walker missed multiple games in each of his first three NFL campaigns with injuries including a sports hernia as well as shoulder, ankle, oblique and calf issues. home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their first injury report ahead of Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks. After being a limited participant in practice all of last week with a back injury, Chiefs starting LT Josh Simmons is back to being a non-participant. The difference this time? Simmons is now being listed with both the back injury and a “personal” designation. You might recall the 2025 NFL season, when Simmons missed four weeks due to a personal family matter. When he returned, Simmons broke his wrist and ultimately played in just eight total games that year. It's unclear what the “personal” designation refers to, but The Athletic's Jesse Newell said Simmons was in the locker room ahead of practice . Here’s a quick breakdown of each team's Week 7 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. I expected this for the veteran , but I don't anticipate him being at risk of missing Sunday's game. home.headline: Chiefs-Seahawks Week 7 Thursday injury report: Rashee Rice stays sidelined
home.blurb: On Thursday, Kansas City placed left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) on the Reserve/Injured list after he didn't practice on Wednesday. The Chiefs explained that Simmons plateaued in his rehabilitation and needed more time to return to 100%. For more information from the team's Head Trainer Rick Burkholder, we covered his statement to local media here . Right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) did not participate in practice again after entering the concussion protocol during the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Moore's participation going forward is dependent on the contracted independent neurologist and completely out of the team and player's hands. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was a limited participant in practice again. Kelce briefly left in Week 6 against the Chargers and was seen multiple times having his ankle taped. Linebacker Cooper McDonald (knee) was a limited participant in practice for the second straight day. McDonald was placed on the team's Reserve/Injured list after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. Although he has been "designated to return," McDonald must be officially added to the active roster by Saturday in order to play against Seattle. The Chiefs seemingly opened a roster spot for McDonald by waiving linebacker Cam Jones on Tuesday. Veteran defensive end Demarcus Lawrence (non-injury related – rest) was a limited participant in practice on Thursday after sitting out on Wednesday. Starting outside linebacker Uchenne Nwosu (hip) popped up on Thursday's injury report as a limited participant after not appearing on the list on Wednesday. Former Missouri quarterback, the backup to Sam Darnold, Drew Lock (right elbow) was a limited participant in practice on both days this week. Wide receiver Rasheed Shaheed (hip), linebacker Tyrice Knight, and guards Anthony Bradford (knee) and Beau Stephens (knee) were full participants in Thursday's practice after limited action on Wednesday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Here’s a look at the odds, the latest movement since Sunday night and a quick preview of this primetime matchup. Even with Jalen Hurts on injured reserve and out for the season, Philly has a shot to pull off an upset against a Dallas defense that is 31st in the NFL EPA/Play. Plus, the Cowboys’ offense looked awful on Sunday night in a loss to Green Bay, which may have caused the move in this line on Monday morning. Cowboys vs. Eagles Betting Preview The Eagles have covered the spread just once in the 2026 season (in their London loss to Jacksonville), so it’s hard to justify betting on them with a backup at quarterback. However, Dallas’ defense remains a bottom three unit in the league, and McKee (215 passing yards in Week 6) was at least able to move the Philly offense. If Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is able to return in Week 7, it could flip these odds even further towards the Eagles. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6. A win for Philly could bump it back up into at least the No. 3 spot in the odds to win the NFC East, but it seems pretty clear that oddsmakers expect Dallas to eventually figure things out and advance as the division winner.
