picks.headline: Eagles vs. Cowboys prediction as Philadelphia adjusts without Jalen Hurts
picks.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys were figured to be the two frontrunners in the NFC East this season, with some even considering the duo as Super Bowl contenders. Just six weeks into the season, both teams are closer to booking vacations than they are preparing for a February trip to Los Angeles. Injuries did a number on the Eagles, claiming Saquon Barkley and many more. Recently, Jalen Hurts was added to that list. The quarterback is done for the year with blood clots . As for Dallas, it's still the defense. And it always has been. In recent weeks, though, the Cowboys offense has become a major problem as well. That isn't a winning combination for Brian Schottenheimer, who has seen his job security come into question lately. Both teams are desperate for a win, but at least the Eagles have a built-in excuse. Dallas will try to right the ship, but can they do it in a hostile Philadelphia environment? Eagles vs Cowboys odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Eagles -3 Moneyline: Eagles -162; Cowboys +136 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Eagles Keys To Victory Stay in the fight. For all intents and purposes, the Eagles season is over after it was revealed Jalen Hurts would miss the remainder of the campaign with blood clots. Injuries have mounted, but there is still talent on this Philadelphia roster. And with the way Dallas is playing, the Eagles just have to stick around long enough to let the Cowboys beat themselves. That leaky defense and anemic offense will give the home team plenty of opportunities to win. The Eagles just have to take them. Cowboys Keys To Victory Show up. On paper, Dallas should run away with this game against an offense that can't possibly keep up. However, the Cowboys looked disinterested in Week 6 and have looked that way for quite some time. This is the perfect get-right spot against a division rival. If the Cowboys don't beat themselves, they'll win the game. Injuries to watch • RB Saquon Barkley • OL Landon Dickerson • DL Jordan Davis • LB Nolan Smith • LB Jaylx Hunt • WR KaVontae Turpin • LB DeMarvion Overshown • LB Dee Winters Eagles vs Cowboys USA TODAY expert picks Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Eagles 23, Cowboys 17 The Eagles are injured. The Cowboys are lifeless. One of them has to win. How's that for a promo? Dallas is clearly the more talented team on paper, but something stinks about this group, and it's hard to pinpoint where the smell is coming from. The defense isn't competitive. The offense appears to be going through the motions. After a rough week for the Eagles, they should be motivated to stop the bleeding and get back in the win column. And what better way to do that than against a hated rival? Even if it's only for a moment, the home team finally gives the fans a reason to smile. Adam Kaufman: Cowboys 24, Eagles 20 Not sure how many times I'm going to put myself in position to be let down by the Cowboys this season, but here we are again. With Jalen Hurts out for the season, the Eagles need Tanner McKee to stabilize an offense that was already having problems. Dallas' vulnerable defense – to put it kindly – gives him an opportunity, especially if Philadelphia can establish the run. On the other side, Dak Prescott's offense has been largely absent each of the last two weeks. But the superior talent undeniably belongs to the Cowboys and, if they can protect the ball, I like them to bounce back in a pivotal division matchup. away.headline: Cowboys Make Announcement on Key Injured Signee
away.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys are trying to get themselves back together again, and while there has been much focus on the coaching, the schemes, and the efforts of the players, one of the overriding shortcomings of this team has been health, plain and simple. The Cowboys had some weakness in the secondary coming into the year, and have not had much luck keeping players on the back line healthy. At different times, Malik Hooker (forearm) and Jalen Thompson (hamstring), two starting safeties, have gone out with injuries, and their backup, PJ Locke, has been on the injured reserve since Week 2 with a porn plantar fascia. But things have been moving in the right direction for the Cowboys and their defensive players. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and cornerback Cobie Durant have returned to practice and are expected to play on Monday against the Eagles. Marist Liufau, out since the preseason with a broken arm, is coming back from the IR, too. Under NFL rules, the Cowboys will have 21 days to activate Locke or put him on the season-ending IR. That means he could be ready to go, at the latest, by Week 10. Cowboys Hoping Defense Improves Before PJ Locke Returns The hope is that the Cowboys defense, rated as one of the worst in the NFL through six weeks, will have improved by then. Already, they looked better in the Sunday night loss to Green Bay last week, but there is more to be done. As team leader Quinnen Williams said on Thursday at practice, the arrow my be pointing up for this unit: "I'm on the right trajectory, right direction to play how I know I can play. But just setting the standard, not only for me, but for this defense in general, and the ability that we have as a unit. … We have the coaching staff and the players to achieve those goals that we want to achieve. away.headline: Cobie Durant Says He Can Do Anything Physically After Returning To Cowboys Practice
away.blurb: FRISCO, Texas — Dallas Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant returned to practice Thursday on a limited basis after missing four games with a hamstring injury, and said there is nothing he cannot do physically as Dallas prepares for Monday night’s game at Philadelphia. “I’m feeling great, man,” Durant said. “I’m a little limited right now, so I’m just taking it one day at a time and staying on top of this hamstring thing because it’s tricky. And just being available. That’s the best thing about this business. The best ability is availability.” Ravens QB Lamar Jackson inches one step closer toward injury return Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing Durant hurt the hamstring in Dallas’ 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 2. He signed with the Cowboys this offseason after four seasons with the Los Angeles Rams . Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said before practice that Durant should get some work. Hamstrings have hit the Cowboys repeatedly this season. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown missed five games with one before returning to full practice Thursday, and safety Alijah Clark and offensive tackle Drew Shelton were both listed with hamstring injuries on Thursday’s report. “I can do anything, honestly,” Durant explained. “I’m just being smart about it.” Cobie Durant On Watching The Dallas Cowboys’ Secondary From The Sideline Durant watched the last four games from the sideline. Rookie safety Caleb Downs was among the players who took snaps in the slot in his place. Offenses get paid too, in Durant’s view, and big plays against the secondary have to be put away quickly. “Things happen, man. It’s the NFL,” Durant said. “They get paid the same way we get paid on defense. Offense get paid, we get paid. So control the controllables. And when things happen, man, you just got to put it behind you and go to the next play.” Durant On Takeaways And Joey Porter Jr. Dallas was the last team in the NFL without an interception until linebacker Dee Winters picked off Jordan Love in the 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Oct. 18. The Cowboys traded for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. on Oct. 1, sending a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to Pittsburgh. Punching at the ball is part of the job for the secondary, according to Durant, and so is getting the ball back to Dak Prescott . “Just creating takeaways, man, getting the ball back to Dak Prescott. Great offense here and that’s our main thing, man,” Durant said. “We just got to create more turnovers, punching at the ball, interceptions, any way we can create a turnover and get the ball back to Dak and let the offense do what they do. Man, we’ll be all right.” Durant believes takeaways come in bunches once a defense gets the first one. Dallas has 1 interception through six games. “I’m a defensive guy, so I say yeah,” Durant said. away.headline: After a week of heavy scrutiny, Caleb Downs will love to hear the latest Dallas Cowboys injury update
away.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys opened PJ Locke's practice window on Friday. And while he's technically a backup safety, his return matters far more for their first-round rookie than you might think. First, the news. Opening Locke's window means he's nearing a return, though it doesn't confirm he'll play on Monday Night Football against the Philadelphia Eagles. It does mean Dallas can activate him to the 53-man roster at any point over the next three weeks. Why a backup safety's return is a big deal So why does a backup's return matter this much? First and foremost, Locke is not just any backup. He’s well-versed in Christian Parker’s scheme and was expected to contribute one way or another from the start. But Locke is a high-quality backup. He's not Markquese Bell, who has struggled filling in at safety and forced the Cowboys into some uncomfortable adjustments. With Locke back soon, and with cornerback Cobie Durant expected to return as well, Dallas will have more options. And more options free up Downs' play style. I understand people calling him out for struggling in the slot. But it's been a snip-snap, snip-snap start for him. Adapting to the NFL is hard enough at one position, and Dallas has been bouncing him between several while playing 98% of the snaps. Durant adds another layer. He could start outside, but he's also played nickel before, and he's a much better option there than Steward. Dallas honestly ran out of bodies in the secondary. I understand the frustration with the entire defense. Still, I'm far, far away from pressing the panic button on Downs, and Locke's return would help him tremendously, whether it comes this week or next. away.headline: Cowboys' Preseason Superstar Could Make NFL Debut Thanks to KaVontae Turpin Injury
away.blurb: The Cowboys have carried five receivers into gamedays for every contest this season. Turpin being ruled out would lessen that number to four, unless they dress Camden Brown, who has remained inactive for every game this season. DeMarvion Overshown Injury Update: Cowboys Star LB Could Return in Week 6 The Dallas Cowboys are dealing with an injury at wide receiver that opens the door for one of the team's preseason superstars to make his NFL debut in Week 7. That injury is to wide receiver and returner KaVontae Turpin, who is dealing with a ribs injury he suffered in Week 6. Turpin did not take part in practice on Thursday. Furthermore, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that Turpin is dealing with "cartilage damage" and will "probably" miss at least this week, when the Cowboys face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night. "Cowboys receiver/returner KaVontae Turpin suffered an injury to his ribs Sunday, and one source believes he's dealing with cartilage damage," Fowler wrote. "He will probably miss this week and go from there," he added. Dallas' offense has sputtered of late . Perhaps the Cowboys should not only dress Brown, who was electric during the preseason, but also give him some snaps. Brown also has special teams experience after playing in that area during the preseason, so that gives him added value and a better chance to finally see the field in Week 7. Camden Brown's electric offseason An undrafted free-agent signing of the Cowboys after the 2026 NFL Draft, Brown was a menace against Dallas defense in camp (that doesn't hold as much weight as it once did with how badly the Cowboys' defense has played, but I digress) and he then carried that into the preseason with electric showings. The 6-foot-2, 204-pound wide receiver tallied three catches for 62 yards and two touchdowns in preseason Week 1 , and followed that up with two catches for 77 yards in the second exhibition contest. “The game’s not too big for him. He does it every day in practice, we see it all the time," head coach Brian Schottenheimer stated . "Really good day, but he’s got to keep stacking what he’s been doing." But it wasn't just about the totals for Brown, who made some "this guy belongs in the league" kinds of catches along the way. Brown cooled off in the final preseason game with just one catch for 27 yards, but he had done enough to state his case and the Cowboys ended up keeping him against all odds because the expectation all offseason was the team would only carry five wideouts with how top-heavy it was. Cowboys fans have been wanting to see Brown all season long after the impressive display he had during the offseason. With Turpin likely to sit, it's time to free Camden Brown and let him play some snaps on offense, too. Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice 🤔 ▶️ Full Rams-Eagles Recap 05:36 The Eagles' running game has suffered greatly in his absence and that of Tank Bigsby, who's on injured reserve. The team combined to have 57 total rushing yards in the defeats to the Carolina Panthers and Jacksonville Jaguars. With quarterback Jalen Hurts likely to miss the remainder of the season, the offense needs to have a steady presence on the ground. Starting in place of Hurts, Tanner McKee went 26-of-45 for 215 yards and a touchdown in Week 6. As backup quarterbacks go, Philadelphia could probably do worse, but there's a massive gulf in quality between Hurts and McKee. Having Barkley in the backfield will take some pressure off McKee. away.headline: Cowboys vs. Eagles Injury Report
away.blurb: "It felt good to be back out there on the field with the guys practicing," Barkley told reporters. Part of Barkley's frustration is that he's never dealt with a hamstring injury before. He's sought out plenty of advice on how to manage it. "You want to be out there and try to help the team," Barkley said. "Hopefully I'll be able to go Monday." "Your play-action pass game gets better and better as you run the football better," Head Coach Nick Sirianni said. "We know we have to play not only complementary football offensively, defensively, special teams, but also within the offense. For your play-action game to create the plays that you want it to create, your run game's got to be going. You've got to be converting on third downs. You've got to be in manageable situations to continue to get reps and plays out there. While Barkley is inching closer to a return, the Eagles were without their top pass catchers – tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) – at practice. Defensively, defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen) remains sidelined, while outside linebacker Nolan Smith is in the concussion protocol. The Dallas Cowboys are preparing to welcome the return of cornerback Cobie Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown back to the lineup. "We play on Monday, so now I've got to wait an extra day, but I'm excited," Overshown said. "I've definitely taken this rehab, this recovery, very serious. I've been trying to get back on the field since the week after I got out. Getting this opportunity to go this week, I'm thankful that I'm still able to get to do what I love." Durant, meanwhile, has also been out due to a hamstring injury incurred in the Week 2 matchup with the Commanders. Durant was limited on Thursday. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, Dallas will not have one of the league's best return specialists in wide receiver KaVontae Turpin, who exited the Week 6 loss to the Packers early with a rib injury. home.headline: Eagles list 24 on injury report as Smith, Wicks and Goedert sit out
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Saquon Barkley’s return to practice gave the Eagles an encouraging sign Thursday, but another lengthy injury report raised concerns about their passing game ahead of Monday night’s matchup against Dallas. Philadelphia listed 24 players, including six who did not participate. DeVonta Smith sat out with a hamstring injury, Dontayvion Wicks was sidelined with an ankle injury, and Dallas Goedert did not practice because of a knee injury. Barkley was listed as limited with his hamstring injury after missing the past two games. NFL Network reported earlier Thursday that he was expected to practice and was in line to play against Dallas. Barkley has rushed for 182 yards on 36 carries this season, averaging 5.1 yards per attempt. Philadelphia also had eight limited participants, including Landon Dickerson, Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Drew Kendall and Tyler Steen. Dickerson was listed with knee and pectoral injuries, while Hunt was listed with knee and ankle injuries. This article originally appeared on Eagles Wire: Eagles list 24 on injury report as Smith, Wicks and Goedert sit out Smith’s absence comes after he caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown in Sunday’s loss to Carolina. Wicks has 19 receptions for 284 yards and a touchdown this season, with 16 catches producing first downs. Their availability will be important as Philadelphia attempts to establish more consistency around quarterback Tanner McKee. Goedert added six receptions for 61 yards against the Panthers , making his status another significant storyline for an offense already operating without Jalen Hurts. Michael Carter, Willie Lampkin and Nolan Smith joined the three pass catchers as nonparticipants. Smith remains listed with a concussion after leaving against Carolina. Among the encouraging developments, Jordan Davis practiced fully after leaving Sunday’s game with shin and thumb injuries. Zack Baun, Marquise Brown, Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers also participated fully. Thursday’s report reflects practice participation, not final availability. The Eagles have two more scheduled practice reports before they can determine game designations in their attempt to end a four-game losing streak.

Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. "Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar," Knox wrote. "Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles." Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline.

home.headline: NFL finds Philadelphia Eagles committed no wrongdoing in Jalen Hurts blood clot saga – ‘was handled appropriately’
home.blurb: The quarterback, 28, has been ruled out for the remainder of the season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. An Eagles statement previously read, “Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team’s flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. “Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia. “On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority.” THE NFL could make the instant replay review process available for viewers on broadcasts later this year, according to reports. home.headline: Philadelphia Eagles sign ex-New York Giants OL Evan Neal
home.blurb: The Alabama product was taken seventh overall by the Giants in 2022 and went on to appear in 29 games with 27 starts, all of them at right tackle. Injuries and recurring struggles in pass protection limited his production over those seasons. Head coach John Harbaugh gave Neal a clean slate this offseason on a one-year deal, only for the team to release him during final roster cuts in August. After a brief stop on the Las Vegas Raiders’ practice squad, Neal worked out for the Eagles on Wednesday, practiced with the team Thursday, and was officially added as a guard. Former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal has landed with the Philadelphia Eagles , who signed the 2022 first-round pick to their practice squad on Thursday. New York moved Neal inside to guard ahead of 2025, but he never took an offensive snap and spent time on injured reserve (IR). The move provides Philadelphia additional depth amid ongoing offensive-line concerns. From the Giants’ perspective, Neal’s arrival in Philadelphia closes another chapter on a high draft investment that never developed into the long-term starter the franchise once expected. New York has continued to reshape its offensive line without him as he searches for a foothold elsewhere.
